Visualisation prior art for disk maps\n\n| Tool | Visual idiom | License | Source |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| **btrfs-heatmap** | Whole physical address space as a PNG laid out on a **Hilbert curve**, so nearby addresses stay nearby in 2-D. Colour = data/metadata/system, brightness = fill ratio. Can make time-lapses. Supports Hilbert, snake and linear walks, and extent-level zoom into block groups. | MIT | [knorrie/btrfs-heatmap](https://github.com/knorrie/btrfs-heatmap), [curves doc](https://github.com/knorrie/btrfs-heatmap/blob/master/doc/curves.md) |\n| **Windows Disk Defragmenter (95–XP), UltraDefrag, Defraggler, MyDefrag** | Grid of cells, one per cluster range, coloured by state (free, contiguous, fragmented, system, MFT). Animated while defragmenting. | various (UltraDefrag GPL) | [UltraDefrag](https://ultradefrag.net/) |\n| **WinDirStat / QDirStat / KDirStat / GrandPerspective** | **Treemaps** of file sizes by directory (logical space, not physical placement). | GPL-3.0 / GPL-2.0 | [windirstat/windirstat](https://github.com/windirstat/windirstat), [shundhammer/qdirstat](https://github.com/shundhammer/qdirstat) |\n| **dust**, **parallel-disk-usage (pdu)** | Terminal bar charts of directory sizes, written in Rust. | Apache-2.0 | [bootandy/dust](https://github.com/bootandy/dust), [KSXGitHub/parallel-disk-usage](https://github.com/KSXGitHub/parallel-disk-usage) |\n| **filefrag** (e2fsprogs) | Per-file extent list (logical → physical, length, flags) through the FIEMAP ioctl. | GPL-2.0 | [filefrag(8)](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man8/filefrag.8.html) |\n| **e2freefrag** | Histogram of free-extent sizes, a free-space fragmentation report. | GPL-2.0 | [e2freefrag(8)](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man8/e2freefrag.8.html) |\n| **debugfs** (`stat`, `blocks`, `ex`, `icheck`, `ffb`) | Interactive inspection of inodes, extent trees and bitmaps. | GPL-2.0 | [debugfs(8)](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man8/debugfs.8.html) |\n| **dumpe2fs** | Per-group layout (superblock backups, bitmaps, inode tables, free counts). | GPL-2.0 | [dumpe2fs(8)](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man8/dumpe2fs.8.html) |\n\n**Ideas for the LFS GitHub Pages viewer:**\n\n1. A **Hilbert-curve block map**, as in btrfs-heatmap: each pixel = one block or cluster, coloured by owner class (superblock, journal, link records, index trees, bitstring indexes, file data, free, *gap-filler doublet links*). Hovering shows block, owner and link id.\n2. A **linear defrag-style strip** for the same data.\n3. **Extent list per file**, as in `filefrag -v`.\n4. **Free-extent histogram**, as in `e2freefrag`.\n5. **Treemap** of logical usage.\n6. **Time-lapse** of a scripted workload (create/append/delete), to show visually that no fragmentation builds up.\n\nThe data can come from a WASM build of the LFS core running a format-and-workload scenario in the browser, or from JSON dumps produced in CI.\n\n---\n\n## Implications for LFS\n\n1. **Architecture: one OS-agnostic core, thin adapters.**\n   - The `lfs-core` crate holds the on-disk format, allocator, journal, links store and indexes. It runs on any `Read+Write+Seek` device (file image, raw device, in-memory, WASM).\n   - Adapters, in priority order:\n     - (a) **Linux/macOS: `fuser`** (MIT). Pure-rust mount on Linux needs no system libs to build. macOS needs macFUSE or FUSE-T at build time unless built with `macos-no-mount`.\n     - (b) **All three OSes: `nfsserve`** (BSD-3) localhost NFSv3. No kernel driver and pure Rust; the best path for macOS without a kext and for CI. Windows needs Pro or higher.\n     - (c) **Windows: WinFsp** for the best NTFS-like semantics. Because winfsp-rs is GPL-3.0, prefer **hand-written Unlicense FFI bindings to `winfsp-x64.dll`**, which WinFsp's FLOSS exception allows since the Unlicense is OSI-approved, or use **`dokan`** (MIT crate, LGPL DLL, no bindgen).\n     - (d) Later: **FSKit** Swift extension wrapping the Rust core (macOS 15.4+), and in-kernel drivers.\n   - RedoxFS (MIT, COW, fuser-based) is the closest existing template.\n2. **CI**:\n   - Core unit and property tests on ubuntu, macos and windows runners.\n   - FUSE mount tests on ubuntu (`modprobe fuse`, `apt install fuse3`; remove the non-setuid `/usr/local/bin/fusermount3`).\n   - WinFsp mount tests on windows (`choco install winfsp` plus a registry check; clang is preinstalled for bindgen if winfsp-sys is used).\n   - On macOS: build-only for FUSE, and NFS (`mount_nfs`) mount tests through `nfsserve`.\n3. **Anti-fragmentation techniques worth copying (simplified):**\n   - **extents** with a large or configurable max length (ext4 is capped at 128 MiB by a 15-bit length field; LFS can use 32- or 64-bit lengths);\n   - **delayed allocation** (allocate at flush, when the size is known);\n   - **per-file preallocation windows** plus **shared small-object arenas** (ext4 `mb_stream_req` = 16 blocks, `mb_group_prealloc` = 512);\n   - **free-space index by size class** (mballoc's largest-free-order and average-fragment-size lists, or a buddy allocator);\n   - **inline data** for tiny files;\n   - **flex_bg-like grouping** of metadata;\n   - **metadata checksums** (crc32c).\n   - ext4 still ages (FAST'17), so the strict \"no fragmentation\" goal needs either **online compaction/relocation** (like `EXT4_IOC_MOVE_EXT`) or the issue's idea: **fill gaps with small doublet links** so free space stays in a few large runs and small objects pack densely.\n4. **Single journal or commit for FS and database.** The JOJ literature (ATC'13, FAST'14 ×2, ATC'15) shows a 58–73 % to 5× penalty from stacked journals. LFS should:\n   - expose **transactions on links and file ranges** to applications, generalising F2FS atomic writes and SQLite's batch-atomic mode;\n   - make the journal **optional and per-file/per-subtree configurable**, as in the adaptive per-file journaling of Shen et al., with modes like ext4's `ordered`, `journal` and `writeback`, plus \"none\" for COW regions;\n   - keep checksummed commit blocks, as in JBD2.\n5. **Index selection rule:** for a link X with k users out of N slots, store its by-source and by-target sets as\n   - an **embedded tree** while `k/N < 1/(p·w)` (= 1/192 for 3×64-bit tree fields),\n   - a **bitstring** above that, with hysteresis (for example, switch back below 1/384).\n   - Better still, decide **per chunk** (Roaring-style: array ≤ C/m entries, bitmap above), so the rule does not drift as N grows.\n   - Make `p`, `w`, the chunk size and the thresholds runtime configuration in the superblock or a mount option. Precedents: Roaring's 4096 and btrfs's free-space-tree conversion.\n6. **Portability:** no advanced FS is native on all three OSes (only FAT32, exFAT and UDF are), so a Rust user-space LFS with adapters for all three fills a real gap. Ship a `mkfs.lfs`/`lfs-mount` CLI per OS and document driver prerequisites (macFUSE/FUSE-T, WinFsp/Dokan, NFS client).\n7. **Viewer:** compile the core to WASM for GitHub Pages. Render a Hilbert-curve block map (btrfs-heatmap), a linear defrag strip, per-file extent lists (filefrag), a free-extent histogram (e2freefrag) and a time-lapse of a workload.\n8. **Licensing:** keep LFS Unlicense. Allowed dependencies are MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD and Unlicense (fuser, nfsserve, dokan, roaring, bitvec, fatfs, ext4-view, redoxfs). Avoid GPL/AGPL crates (winfsp-rs, windows-projfs, ZeroFS, tvix) in the shipped binary, or isolate them behind an optional, clearly labelled feature.\n"

The sources tree is ordered by (source, target), the targets tree by (target, source). `size` is the plain subtree count, and 0 means \"not in the tree\".\n- **Rust vs C# trees:** Rust uses only the non-recursive version. In C#, \"Default\" and even \"Recursionless\" both pick the recursive version in the united store, but the bytes on disk are the same.\n- **C# AVL option:** it packs balance and thread bits into bits 0–4 of `size`, so its files are not compatible with the size-balanced ones.\n- **Free list:**\n  - it is a circular list threaded through freed slots (`source` = previous, `target` = next);\n  - freed slots are reused most-recent-first;\n  - deleting the last link shrinks `allocated`.\n- **Growth:** steps of 2^20 links (64 MiB for u64).\n  - C# cuts the file back to `(allocated + 1) * 64` bytes on close.\n  - Rust never shrinks the file.\n  - Rust doublets 0.8.0 with the standard file mapping wipes the database to zeros on reopen (mem-rs#36); link-cli works around this.\n- **Reserved values:** `null` = 0. `continue`, `break`, `skip`, `any`, `itself` and `error` are the top six values of the internal range.\n- **External references:** when enabled, the internal range is `1..=2^63-1`, and an external raw number `n` is stored as `-n` (top bit set).\n- **Bit strings:** `BitString` exists only as an in-memory set of 64-bit words. It has 96 golden test vectors and codecs in 8 languages. The links-queue \"BLN\" format is a different thing, and link-cli rejected it for stores.\n- **Header byte:**\n  - bits 7–4 are the version (`0001`);\n  - bits 3–2 are log2 of the width, for the compact layout;\n  - bit 1 selects the explicit layout;\n  - bit 0 enables external references.\n- **Compact layout:** a LEB128 count followed by doublets; the empty packet is `10 00`.\n- **Explicit layout:** sections, each with a shape, an optional gap, an optional extra and a count.\n- External values are stored as `2^w - v`, the same negation trick as the doublets store.\n- Packed widths are chosen by a dynamic-programming pass and never cost more than uniform widths.\n- **Store archive:** a links packet that keeps holes as gaps, followed by a names packet of `address code-point...`. Caveats: in unified mode tree slots are mandatory (already paid) — savings only with split/variable layout; N grows → use chunked bitstrings; hysteresis like btrfs; time break-even earlier: enumeration tree k·M cache misses vs N/64 sequential words → ρ > 1/(64·M) (M≈50–200); membership O(log k) vs O(1); count via Size O(1) vs popcount unless cached.\n   - Roaring format spec https://github.com/RoaringBitmap/RoaringFormatSpec: array ≤4096, bitset 8KB, run containers 2+4x bytes; paper \"Better bitmap performance with Roaring bitmaps\" (Chambi, Lemire et al.). Without root it falls back to the setuid `fusermount3` program.\n  - On the Ubuntu runner, mount tests work after `sudo modprobe fuse; sudo chmod 666 /dev/fuse; apt install fuse3`. Newer images also ship a non-setuid `/usr/local/bin/fusermount3`, which rclone's CI deletes.\n- **macOS:** `fuser` against macFUSE (`brew install --cask macfuse`; pkgconf is preinstalled).\n  - It only builds without macFUSE if you use the `macos-no-mount` feature, which can't mount.\n  - Mounting in CI is effectively impossible because the kernel extension needs interactive approval and a reboot. fuser's own macOS CI only builds.\n  - Alternatives:\n    - FUSE-T: no kernel extension, works over local NFS/SMB, but needs a commercial licence to redistribute.\n    - FSKit: macOS 15.4+, requires a Swift app extension.\n    - `nfsserve` with the built-in `mount_nfs`.\n- **Windows:**\n  - `winfsp` 0.13.2 is **GPL-3.0**, which clashes with the Unlicense goal. At runtime you run `choco install winfsp`, then check the registry InstallDir key because choco can report success without installing.\n  - Options without the GPL problem: hand-written Unlicense bindings to the WinFsp DLL (WinFsp's own licence has an open-source exception that covers the Unlicense), or `dokan` 0.3.1. The `dokan` crate is MIT and builds its import library with `cc` (no libclang), but it is stale (last release 2022) and the Dokan driver is LGPL.\n  - ProjFS (Windows Projected File System) can't host a real file system.\n- **All three:** `nfsserve` 0.11.0 (BSD-3) is a pure-Rust NFSv3 server with no build dependencies. Windows needs the NFS client, which Home editions lack, and the crate's README calls Windows support only partial.\n- **Recommended shape:** an OS-independent `lfs-core` crate tested on all three runners against a file-backed device, plus thin adapters. RedoxFS (MIT, copy-on-write, uses `fuser`) is the closest existing template.\n\n**When a bitstring index beats a tree**\n- For a link X used by k of N link slots, an embedded tree costs `p·w·k` bits (p index words per member, w-bit words) and a bitstring costs N bits.\n- **Break-even density: ρ\\* = k/N = 1/(p·w).** For 3×64-bit tree fields that is **1/192 ≈ 0.52%**; for 32-bit words 1/96; for a sorted array 1/64.\n- Roaring bitmaps use the same rule (65536 / 16 = 4096). btrfs's free-space tree switches extents to bitmaps on the same space comparison, with a 100-item margin to stop it flipping back and forth.\n- Caveats:\n  - In the unified layout the six index words are already paid for in every record, so a bitstring only saves space with a split or variable-size layout.\n  - N keeps growing, so decide per chunk, Roaring-style, rather than against all of N.\n  - Use a gap between the switch-up and switch-down thresholds (e.g. up at 1/192, back at 1/384).\n  - For enumeration speed the bitstring wins much earlier, roughly at ρ > 1/(64·M), where M is the cost of one random read in sequential word reads. That is my estimate and needs benchmarking.\n- Make p, w, chunk size and both thresholds configurable.\n\n**ext4 anti-fragmentation techniques worth copying**\n- Extents. ext4 caps an extent at 32768 blocks (128 MiB at 4 KiB), and LFS can use wider length fields.\n- Delayed allocation.\n- mballoc-style placement: per-file preallocation, with small files (under 16 blocks) packed into shared 512-block groups. Free space is indexed by largest free size and average fragment size.\n- An in-memory buddy cache built from the on-disk bitmaps.\n- Grouping metadata together (flex_bg) and keeping data near its inode and directory.\n- Inline data for tiny files (under 60 bytes, or about 160 in a 256-byte inode).\n- crc32c checksums on metadata.\n- ext4 still ages badly: reads can slow 2–30× after hundreds of git pulls (Conway et al., FAST'17). So a real no-fragmentation goal needs online relocation (like ext4's `EXT4_IOC_MOVE_EXT`) or the issue's idea of filling gaps with small links.\n\n**Double journaling**\n- Stacking a file system journal under a database journal costs 58–73% (Shen et al., FAST'14), and up to 5× in the WALDIO paper (USENIX ATC'15).\n- It goes away when the database keeps its recovery data inside its own structure, or when the file system offers atomic writes. SQLite already does this on F2FS.\n- LFS should share one commit mechanism between files and links, and make journaling optional per file, with modes like ext4's ordered, journal and writeback.\n\n**Portability:** only FAT32, exFAT and UDF are read-write natively on all three OSes, and none has journaling or checksums. NTFS is read-only on macOS, and ext4, btrfs, APFS and ReFS are each native on one OS."

RedoxFS (MIT, copy-on-write, uses `fuser`) is the closest existing template.\n\n**When a bitstring index beats a tree**\n- For a link X used by k of N link slots, an embedded tree costs `p·w·k` bits (p index words per member, w-bit words) and a bitstring costs N bits.\n- **Break-even density: ρ\\* = k/N = 1/(p·w).** For 3×64-bit tree fields that is **1/192 ≈ 0.52%**; for 32-bit words 1/96; for a sorted array 1/64.\n- Roaring bitmaps use the same rule (65536 / 16 = 4096). btrfs's free-space tree switches extents to bitmaps on the same space comparison, with a 100-item margin to stop it flipping back and forth.\n- Caveats:\n  - In the unified layout the six index words are already paid for in every record, so a bitstring only saves space with a split or variable-size layout.\n  - N keeps growing, so decide per chunk, Roaring-style, rather than against all of N.\n  - Use a gap between the switch-up and switch-down thresholds (e.g. up at 1/192, back at 1/384).\n  - For enumeration speed the bitstring wins much earlier, roughly at ρ > 1/(64·M), where M is the cost of one random read in sequential word reads. That is my estimate and needs benchmarking.\n- Make p, w, chunk size and both thresholds configurable.\n\n**ext4 anti-fragmentation techniques worth copying**\n- Extents. ext4 caps an extent at 32768 blocks (128 MiB at 4 KiB), and LFS can use wider length fields.\n- Delayed allocation.\n- mballoc-style placement: per-file preallocation, with small files (under 16 blocks) packed into shared 512-block groups. Free space is indexed by largest free size and average fragment size.\n- An in-memory buddy cache built from the on-disk bitmaps.\n- Grouping metadata together (flex_bg) and keeping data near its inode and directory.\n- Inline data for tiny files (under 60 bytes, or about 160 in a 256-byte inode).\n- crc32c checksums on metadata.\n- ext4 still ages badly: reads can slow 2–30× after hundreds of git pulls (Conway et al., FAST'17). So a real no-fragmentation goal needs online relocation (like ext4's `EXT4_IOC_MOVE_EXT`) or the issue's idea of filling gaps with small links.\n\n**Double journaling**\n- Stacking a file system journal under a database journal costs 58–73% (Shen et al., FAST'14), and up to 5× in the WALDIO paper (USENIX ATC'15).\n- It goes away when the database keeps its recovery data inside its own structure, or when the file system offers atomic writes. SQLite already does this on F2FS.\n- LFS should share one commit mechanism between files and links, and make journaling optional per file, with modes like ext4's ordered, journal and writeback.\n\n**Portability:** only FAT32, exFAT and UDF are read-write natively on all three OSes, and none has journaling or checksums. NTFS is read-only on macOS, and ext4, btrfs, APFS and ReFS are each native on one OS.",

Little-endian field helpers and CRC-32 used by every on-disk structure.\n//!\n//! Key Technical Concepts:\n   - **Doublets united layout** (verified in the research doc; byte-compatible target):\n     - Header in record 0: allocated, reserved, free, first_free, root_as_source, root_as_target, last_free, reserved8 (=0).\n     - Record i at offset 64*i: source, target, left_as_source, right_as_source, size_as_source, left_as_target, right_as_target, size_as_target.\n     - Source tree ordered by (source, target); target tree by (target, source).\n     - Size-balanced trees with plain size; size 0 means not in the tree. Links with source 0 or target 0 are not attached to that tree.\n   - **Free list:**\n     - Circular doubly-linked list with prev = source, next = target.\n     - `is_unused(i) = if i<=allocated && first_free != i {size_as_source==0 && source!=0} else {true}`.\n     - Create takes first_free (detach), else allocated += 1. New link is (0,0), then update.\n     - Delete: update(i, 0, 0) detaches it from the trees. If i < allocated, attach_as_first (LIFO). If i == allocated, decrement allocated and pop trailing unused slots.\n     - External refs are stored as 2^64 - n (top bit set); internal range 1..2^63-1.\n     - Rust doublets 0.8 FileMapped wipes the db on reopen (mem-rs#36), so compatibility tests should use doublets heap/in-memory storage built from bytes, or work around it.\n     - Doublets split layout: data part 16 B (source, target); index part 64 B (root/left/right/size for sources, then the same for targets), with the header in index slot 0. Problem Solving — detailed design decisions (to implement):\n   - **On-disk layout:**\n     - Block 0 is the superblock: magic \"LINKSFS\\0\", version, block_size (min 1024, power of 2), total_blocks, journal_start and journal_blocks, layout, name_encoding, commit seq, links header (allocated, free, first_free, root_s, root_t, last_free), root inode link, runtime-config var-blob handle.\n     - 21 array descriptors (table_start, table_blocks, chunk_count): 0 links data, 1 links index (split), 2 inodes, 3 usage handles, 4..=20 var classes 16B..1MB. CRC32 at the end of the block.\n     - Then the journal region, then the dynamic area. The superblock is authoritative for the links header; it is mirrored into united record 0 (and split index record 0) for doublets compatibility.\n   - **No on-disk bitmap:** the allocation map is derived at mount from all owners (superblock, journal, chunk tables, chunks, inode extents). All metadata is held in memory.\n   - **Space allocator (space.rs):**\n     - Used bitset, `BTreeMap<start,len>` of free extents, and `BTreeSet<(len,start)>` for best-fit.\n     - Methods: allocate(len, policy BestFit/FirstFit), allocate_at(start, len), is_free, mark_used.\n     - `free` releases blocks allocated since the last commit (\"fresh\") immediately; other blocks are pending until commit. commit() releases pending blocks and clears fresh.\n   - **ChunkedArray (chunked.rs):**\n     - Fixed-size records in chunks of `chunk_blocks` contiguous blocks. Chunk table = u64 block pointers in its own extent, which doubles when it grows.\n     - Methods: record/record_mut (with dirty tracking), grow, relocate(chunk, new_block), dirty_blocks() → Vec<(block, bytes)>, descriptor, load, extents.\n   - **Commit/journal (journal.rs):**\n     - Dirty blocks that are fresh (free in the committed state) are written directly. Overwrites of live blocks go through the journal.\n     - Journal tx: header block (magic \"LFSJRNL\\0\", seq), descriptor block(s) (\"LFSJDESC\", seq, count, target block list), data blocks, commit block (\"LFSJCMIT\", seq, crc32).\n     - Order: sync, then checkpoint in place, sync, then bump the header seq.\n     - Replay on mount if the tx is valid.\n     - Modes: off / metadata (ordered: data written directly) / full (data overwrites journaled too, split into journal-sized txs).\n     - Auto-commit when live-dirty blocks approach journal capacity. Compaction runs in small commits.\n   - **Files:**\n     - One contiguous extent per file. Inode record of 64 bytes: mode u32, nlink u32, uid u32, gid u32, size u64, start u64, blocks u64, mtime i64 ns, ctime i64 ns, atime i64 ns.\n     - Growth order: extend in place with the growth factor, otherwise the minimum → evict movable chunks in the target range → relocate the file → compact() (slide objects left) → ENOSPC.\n     - Zero-fill the gaps between old size and the write offset. Truncate releases tail blocks.\n   - **Links store:**\n     - Layouts: United (64 B doublets-compatible, doublets free list exactly), Split (16 B data + 48 B index records), DataOnly (16 B, no embedded index).\n     - Split and DataOnly mark free links as (0,0) with an in-memory free set.\n     - Uniqueness of (source, target) is enforced: create on an existing pair → Exists; get_or_create returns the existing link.\n     - API: create, update, delete, search(s,t), each/count with optional index/source/target, get_or_create.\n   - **SBT (sbt.rs):** a generic trait over nodes with left/right/size get/set and `key(n)->(u64,u64,u64)`, where the key is (primary, secondary, index) as a tie-break.\n     - Recursive classic SBT insert with maintain; remove with remove-min replacement plus maintain; rotations.\n     - Guards: size(0) = 0.\n     - Range enumeration with pruning. Count by prefix via rank(k) = number of keys < k (handle u64::MAX overflow).\n     - Reused for the embedded trees and for per-link trees in var blobs (24-byte nodes, swap-remove with a parent search).\n   - **FS schema:**\n     - Points 1..5 are the binary-LiNo markers; LFS type points are 6 FILE, 7 DIR, 8 SYMLINK.\n     - Inode `I = (TYPE, ext(slot))`. Name `N = (STRING, cons chain of ext(code points))`, deduplicated. The format option name_encoding is chars (exact binary-LiNo) or packed (7 bytes of UTF-8 per external).\n     - Entry `E = (dir, N)`; binding `B = (E, child)`; symlink target = the link `(I, N)`.\n     - The parent is derived as source(source(B)), where B has target = the child dir.\n     - Readdir enumerates source=dir. Rename updates E. Hard links add E/B pairs. GC removes unused name chains.\n     - Slot→link map is built at mount. ino 1 maps to the root link.\n   - **Optional index:**\n     - Modes: off / tree / bitstring / adaptive. Per link there are two handles (source role, target role) in the usage-handles array. A handle encodes kind/class/slot.\n     - Bitstring: bit L set iff link L uses X. Adaptive switching uses a threshold of auto = 1/192 or an explicit %, with hysteresis. The bitstring is capped at 1 MB (beyond that use a tree).\n   - **Var store:** classes 2^4..2^20 bytes, each a ChunkedArray. A u32 length prefix; length 0 means a free slot.\n   - **Config (config.rs):**\n     - Format options: block_size, layout, name_encoding, journal_blocks.\n     - Runtime config: journal (off/metadata/full), commit-every, alloc (best-fit/first-fit), gap-fill, growth-percent, index (off/tree/bitstring/adaptive), bitstring-threshold (auto/%), hysteresis-percent, auto-compact, atime, read-only, protect-structure.\n     - Text is parsed as LiNo: accept `(key: value)` and `(key value)`, including nested. Persisted as a var blob. Overridable via `--config file.lino`, `-o key=value`, and `/.lfs/config`.\n   - **Time abstraction:** a `now` fn that is overridable (SystemTime normally; returns 0 on wasm32 unless the web crate sets it).\n   - **Map export:** segments (superblock, journal, chunk tables, link/index/inode/usage/var chunks, file data, preallocated, free) as hand-written JSON.\n   - **CLI:** mkfs, info, map, put, get, ls, mkdir, rm, mv, cat, links (link-cli-like), config, fsck, mount, export-links, import-links, compact. Raw link edits on FS-structural links are refused unless `--force`.\n   - **Drivers:** driver/fuse.rs (Mutex<Fs>) and driver/dokan.rs.\n   - **WASM visualizer:** standalone crate web/ with its own `[workspace]`. A Simulator API (create/append/delete/mkdir/map_json/links_json/stats/set_config/compact/load_image) plus a canvas JS UI. The\nheader lives in index slot 0.\n\n- [`DR/doublets/src/mem/split/data_part.rs#L5`](https://github.com/linksplatform/doublets-rs/blob/02b3c9bf073e7a182acd24ac7ac6e652bebf7ee0/doublets/src/mem/split/data_part.rs#L5)\n- [`DR/doublets/src/mem/split/index_part.rs#L5`](https://github.com/linksplatform/doublets-rs/blob/02b3c9bf073e7a182acd24ac7ac6e652bebf7ee0/doublets/src/mem/split/index_part.rs#L5)\n- C#: `Memory/Split/RawLinkDataPart.cs` and `RawLinkIndexPart.cs` use the same orders.\n\nDataPart (16 B per link, data file offset `16 * i`):\n\n| Off | W | Field |\n|---:|---:|---|\n| 0 | 8 | `source` |\n| 8 | 8 | `target` |\n\nIndexPart (64 B per link, index file offset `64 * i`; slot 0 is the `LinksHeader`):\n\n| Off | W | Field | Meaning |\n|---:|---:|---|---|\n| 0  | 8 | `root_as_source` | root of the **internal** tree of links whose source = this link, keyed by target |\n| 8  | 8 | `left_as_source` | this link as a node of `IndexPart[self.source].root_as_source`'s tree |\n| 16 | 8 | `right_as_source` | \" |\n| 24 | 8 | `size_as_source` | \" |\n| 32 | 8 | `root_as_target` | root of the internal tree of links whose target = this link, keyed by source |\n| 40 | 8 | `left_as_target` | |\n| 48 | 8 | `right_as_target` | |\n| 56 | 8 | `size_as_target` | |\n\nSplit therefore has **per-link usage trees** (internal) plus **two global trees**\nrooted in the header (external) for references outside the internal range.\n\n- C# routes a reference to the external tree when\n  `Constants.ExternalReferencesRange.Contains(value)` (`SplitMemoryLinksBase.cs` ~L629–L680).\n- Rust split instead uses `is_virtual(link) = is_unused(link)`\n  ([`DR/doublets/src/mem/split/store.rs#L345`](https://github.com/linksplatform/doublets-rs/blob/02b3c9bf073e7a182acd24ac7ac6e652bebf7ee0/doublets/src/mem/split/store.rs#L345)).\n  That means unallocated or freed indices go to the external trees.\n- **These two rules differ.** Rust and C# split files are therefore *not\n  guaranteed* to be interchangeable when references point at unallocated or\n  external values. **[verified divergence; impact on real files UNVERIFIED]**\n- C# split has an optional `useLinkedList` mode for the internal sources index.\n  In Rust, `USE_LIST = false` and the list path hits `todo!()`.\n- C# chooses the smaller of the two internal trees for `(s,t)` lookups\n  (`CountUsages(source) > CountUsages(target)`).\n\n### 1.4 Free (\"unused\") list [verified]\n\nThe free list is an absolute circular doubly-linked list\n(`trees-rs/src/lists/absolute_circular_linked_list.rs`). It is threaded\n**through the freed records themselves**:\n\n- `first = header.first_free`, `last = header.last_free`, `size = header.free`;\n- `prev(slot) = slot.source` and `next(slot) = slot.target`;\n- see `DR/doublets/src/mem/unit/generic/unused_links.rs`.\n\nA slot is treated as unused when:\n\n```text\nis_unused(i) = if i <= allocated && first_free != i {\n                   size_as_source == 0 && source != 0     // united\n               } else { true }\n```\n\nIn split, the same check uses `index.size_as_target == 0 && data.source != 0`.\nIn C#, `IsUnusedLink` is `FirstFreeLink == i || (SizeAsSource == 0 && Source != 0)`.\n\n**Note:** a live point link `(i: i i)` always has `size_as_source >= 1` because\nit is in the tree, so the test is unambiguous. A freed slot that is the *only*\nfree entry has `prev = next = itself`. That is why `first_free == i` is checked\nseparately.\n\n### 1.5 Create / delete / grow algorithms [verified]\n\nCreate:\n[`DR/doublets/src/mem/unit/store.rs#L452`](https://github.com/linksplatform/doublets-rs/blob/02b3c9bf073e7a182acd24ac7ac6e652bebf7ee0/doublets/src/mem/unit/store.rs#L452)\n\n```rust\nlet mut free = header.first_free;\nif free == constants.null {\n    let max_inner = *constants.internal_range.end();\n    if header.allocated >= max_inner { return Err(LinksError::LimitReached(max_inner)); }\n    if header.allocated >= header.reserved - T::from_byte(1) {\n        let new_cap = self.mem.allocated().len() + self.reserve_step;\n        let mem = crate::mem::resize_mem(&mut self.mem, new_cap)?.leak();\n        self.update_mem(mem);\n        let reserved = self.mem.allocated().len();\n        let header = self.mut_header();\n        header.reserved = T::try_from(reserved).expect(\"always ok\");\n    }\n    let header = self.mut_header();\n    header.allocated = header.allocated + T::from_byte(1);\n    free = header.allocated;\n} else {\n    self.unused.detach(free);   // reuse most recently freed slot (LIFO via attach_as_first)\n}\n// new link is (free: 0 0); caller then calls update(free, s, t)\n```\n\nDelete:\n[`store.rs#L543`](https://github.com/linksplatform/doublets-rs/blob/02b3c9bf073e7a182acd24ac7ac6e652bebf7ee0/doublets/src/mem/unit/store.rs#L543)\n\n1. Call `update(index, 0, 0)`, which detaches the link from both trees.\n2. If `index < allocated`, call `unused.attach_as_first(index)`.\n3. If `index == allocated`, decrement `allocated`, then keep popping trailing\n   unused slots off the free list. This means the store **shrinks its\n   high-water mark**, and never leaves holes at the end.\n\nUpdate: detach from the source and target trees (when the old value ≠ 0),\nwrite the fields, then attach to the trees rooted at `header.root_as_source` /\n`root_as_target`.\n\nGrowth and initialisation:\n\n- **Rust:**\n  - `DEFAULT_PAGE_SIZE = 8*1024` items;\n  - `SIZE_STEP = 2^20` items, i.e. **64 MiB per step for u64 united**;\n  - `init()` resizes to `max(reserve_step, allocated)` and sets `reserved = len - 1`.\n    The `create` path sets `reserved = len`, so there is an **off-by-one inconsistency**.\n    It is harmless because the check is `allocated >= reserved - 1`.\n- **C#:**\n  - `DefaultLinksSizeStep = LinkSizeInBytes * 1024 * 1024` bytes, which is 2^20 links\n    ([`UnitedMemoryLinksBase.cs#L52`](https://github.com/linksplatform/Data.Doublets/blob/f8c521e539935e670f4f484cf451857d2bd3e693/csharp/Platform.Data.Doublets/Memory/United/Generic/UnitedMemoryLinksBase.cs#L52));\n  - `Init`: `UsedCapacity = Allocated*LinkSize + HeaderSize` and\n    `ReservedLinks = (ReservedCapacity - HeaderSize) / LinkSize` (L175–L186);\n  - on growth: `ReservedLinks = ReservedCapacity / LinkSize` (L529).\n- **File size on disk:**\n  - C# `FileMappedResizableDirectMemory` sets the file size to `ReservedCapacity`\n    while it is open. On dispose it **truncates the file to `UsedCapacity`**,\n    i.e. `(allocated + 1) * 64` bytes for u64\n    ([`Memory/.../FileMappedResizableDirectMemory.cs`](https://github.com/linksplatform/Memory/blob/bf31e5d40174919e515bf52917219a3b67bdeac4/csharp/Platform.Memory/FileMappedResizableDirectMemory.cs)).\n    On open it rounds the reservation up to a multiple of the step.\n  - Rust `mem-rs::FileMapped` grows with `set_len` plus a remap, and on drop only\n    calls `sync_all`. It **does not truncate**, so Rust files stay at whole multiples\n    of the step (≥ 64 MiB).\n- **Known Rust persistence bug:** upstream `RawMem::grow_filled` zero-fills the whole\n  newly mapped range, including bytes already on disk. Reopening a file-mapped DB\n  therefore *zeroes it*. link-cli works around this with `PersistentFileMapped`\n  (`LC/rust/src/storage/file_mem.rs`, using `grow_filled_exact`). Upstream report:\n  linksplatform/mem-rs#36. **LFS must not use plain `FileMapped` with doublets 0.8.0.**",

Problem Solving — design decisions to implement:\n   - **Links store (links/mod.rs), planned API:**\n     - Helpers: `external(v)`, `as_external(raw)`, `is_external(raw)` (raw ≥ 2^63), `is_internal`.\n     - Constants: markers 1..5; type points 6 FILE, 7 DIR, 8 SYMLINK.\n     - `Header{allocated,reserved,free,first_free,root_s,root_t,last_free}`.\n     - Methods: create(s,t) (rejects (0,0); internal refs must exist; Exists if the pair is present), create_point(), update(i,s,t) (detach old → set → attach), delete(i) (Busy if referenced by other links), get(i), exists, search(s,t), each_source/each_target(X, f), count_source/target, get_or_create, and iteration over live links.\n     - United uses the doublets free list exactly. Split/DataOnly use an in-memory free_set (rebuilt from (0,0) records at load); when deleting the top slot, decrement allocated and pop trailing free slots.\n     - Header is mirrored into record 0 (united) or index 0 (split); superblock is authoritative. Shrink chunks at commit.\n     - Query routing:\n       - United: global trees.\n       - Split: per-link tree for internal ends, global tree for externals. search(s,t): s internal → per-link tree of s, range (t,0,0)..(t,MAX,MAX); else t internal → per-link target tree; else global.\n       - DataOnly: optional var index when enabled, else scan. A RAM-only `orphans: HashMap<(s,t),id>` covers links whose ends are both non-internal (e.g. the chain end `(ext(c), 0)`).\n   - **Optional usage index (links/usage.rs):**\n     - Usage-handles ChunkedArray of 16 B per link (handle_s, handle_t), plus a VarStore. Handle kinds: 1 tree, 2 bitstring.\n     - Tree blob: u32 count at payload 0, u32 root at 4, nodes from offset 12 or 16 (choose consistently). Each node is 24 B: link u64, left u32, right u32, size u32, pad. Key = (other end, link, 0). Removal is swap-remove with a parent fix.\n     - Bitstring blob: u32 popcount plus pad; bit L means link L uses X.\n     - Adaptive: switch to bitstring when n/N ≥ threshold (and the bitstring stays ≤ 1 MB); back to tree when below threshold·hysteresis%. Rebuild everything on a runtime mode change. Only internal ends get handles.\n   - **FS schema:**\n     - Inode link I = (TYPE, ext(slot)); ino = slot+1, root is slot 0.\n     - Name N = (3, chain) with chain cells (ext(cp), rest) ending in (ext(cn), 0), deduplicated. Packed encoding: value = len<<56 | up to 7 UTF-8 bytes.\n     - Entry E = (dir, N); binding B = (E, child); symlink S = (I, N_target).\n     - readdir: source=dir → E → source=E → B. Parent: target=D → B → source(source(B)).\n     - Rename updates E. Hard link adds a new E/B pair. nlink = bindings targeting I.\n     - Name GC: delete N if unused, then walk the chain deleting unused cells.\n     - Slot→link map is built at mount. A virtual `/.lfs/` holds config, map.json, links and stats.\n     - Inode record of 64 B: mode u32, nlink u32, uid u32, gid u32, size u64, start u64, blocks u64, mtime/ctime/atime i64 ns.\n   - **File data:**\n     - One contiguous extent per file. Writes to fresh blocks go directly to disk; overwrites of committed blocks go direct in metadata mode and into a cache (journaled at commit) in full mode.\n     - Reads check the cache. Drop cache entries when a range is freed.\n     - Zero-fill gaps. Growth order: extend in place with the growth factor → evict movable chunks → relocate the file → compact → ENOSPC.\n   - **Commit:**\n     1. Place all arrays.\n     2. Build the superblock (block 0, with CRC and commit_seq).\n     3. Collect writes from the arrays, the superblock and cached data.\n     4. Fresh blocks are written directly; sync.\n     5. Live blocks go through a journal tx when the journal is on, otherwise in place.\n     6. Sync, checkpoint in place, sync, then `space.commit()`.\n   - **Journal:**\n     - Region at blocks 1..=J. Tx layout: descriptor block(s) (magic \"LFSJDESC\", seq, count, targets), then data blocks, then a commit block (\"LFSJCMIT\", seq, crc32). No header block.\n     - Replay on mount iff the tx is valid and tx.seq == sb.seq+1, or the superblock CRC is invalid and the tx contains block 0. Replay is idempotent.\n     - An oversize tx is split into non-atomic pieces (documented). Auto-commit when live dirty blocks exceed journal capacity/2. Default journal size: max(64, total/64), capped at 4096.\n   - **Superblock:**\n     - Magic \"LINKSFS\\0\", version, block_size, total_blocks, journal start/blocks, layout, name_encoding, commit seq, links header, root inode link, config var-blob handle.\n     - Array descriptors: 0 links data, 1 links index, 2 inodes, 3 usage handles, 4..=20 var classes (plus anything else needed). CRC32 at the end.\n     - There is no on-disk bitmap; space is rebuilt from the owners at mount.\n   - **Remaining components:**\n     - CLI: mkfs, info, map, put, get, ls, mkdir, rm, mv, cat, links, config, fsck, mount, export-links, import-links, compact.\n     - Drivers: driver/fuse.rs and driver/dokan.rs.\n     - WASM visualizer: web/ crate with its own workspace, deployed via deploy-docs, with Playwright screenshots.\n     - CI jobs: Linux FUSE mount test, Windows Dokan test, macOS build with macFUSE.\n\n6. < 2^63`).\n#[must_use]\npub fn external(value: u64) -> u64 {\n    debug_assert!(value < EXTERNAL_ZERO);\n    encode_external(value, 8)\n}\n\n/// External value of a raw cell, if it is an external reference.\n#[must_use]\npub fn as_external(raw: u64) -> Option<u64> {\n    decode_external(raw, 8)\n}\n\n/// Whether a raw cell is an external reference.\n#[must_use]\npub const fn is_external(raw: u64) -> bool {\n    raw >= EXTERNAL_ZERO\n}\n\n/// Whether a raw cell is a (non-null) link index.\n#[must_use]\npub const fn is_internal(raw: u64) -> bool {\n    raw != 0 && raw < EXTERNAL_ZERO\n}\n\n/// Formats a raw cell: `12` for links, `$7` for externals.\n#[must_use]\npub fn format_ref(raw: u64) -> String {\n    as_external(raw).map_or_else(|| raw.to_string(), |value| format!(\"${value}\"))\n}\n\n/// Parses `12` or `$7` into a raw cell.\npub fn parse_ref(text: &str) -> Result<u64> {\n    let text = text.trim();\n    let (value, ext) = text.strip_prefix('$').map_or((text, false), |rest| (rest, true));\n    let value: u64 = value.parse().map_err(|_| Error::invalid(format!(\"bad reference {text:?}\")))?;\n    if value >= EXTERNAL_ZERO {\n        return Err(Error::invalid(format!(\"reference {text} is out of range\")));\n    }\n    Ok(if ext { external(value) } else { value })\n}\n\n/// The links header (doublets `LinksHeader` without `reserved`).\n#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct Header {\n    /// Highest allocated link index.\n    pub allocated: u64,\n    /// Number of free slots below `allocated`.\n    pub free: u64,\n    /// First slot of the free list (united layout).\n    pub first_free: u64,\n    /// Root of the global sources tree.\n    pub root_as_source: u64,\n    /// Root of the global targets tree.\n    pub root_as_target: u64,\n    /// Last slot of the free list (united layout).\n    pub last_free: u64,\n}\n\nimpl Header {\n    /// Serialized size.\n    pub const SIZE: usize = 48;\n\n    /// Writes the header.\n    pub fn write(&self, bytes: &mut [u8]) {\n        let cells = [\n            self.allocated,\n            self.free,\n            self.first_free,\n            self.root_as_source,\n            self.root_as_target,\n            self.last_free,\n        ];\n        for (index, cell) in cells.iter().enumerate() {\n            crate::codec::put_u64(bytes, index * 8, *cell);\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Reads a header.\n    #[must_use]\n    pub fn read(bytes: &[u8]) -> Self {\n        let cell = |index: usize| crate::codec::get_u64(bytes, index * 8);\n        Self {\n            allocated: cell(0),\n            free: cell(1),\n            first_free: cell(2),\n            root_as_source: cell(3),\n            root_as_target: cell(4),\n            last_free: cell(5),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// One link.\n#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]\npub struct Link {\n    /// Index.\n    pub index: u64,\n    /// Source cell.\n    pub source: u64,\n    /// Target cell.\n    pub target: u64,\n}\n\n/// The links store.\n#[derive(Clone, Debug)]\npub struct Links {\n    /// Records with the embedded 2],\n}\n\nconst fn role_index(role: Role) -> usize {\n    match role {\n        Role::Source => 0,\n        Role::Target => 1,\n    }\n}\n\nconst ROLES: [Role; 2] = [Role::Source, Role::Target];\nconst MAX_KEY: (u64, u64, u64) = (u64::MAX, u64::MAX, u64::MAX);\n\nimpl Links {\n    /// An empty store.\n    #[must_use]\n    pub fn new(layout: Layout, block_size: usize) -> Self {\n        let mut links = Self {\n            records: Records::new(layout, block_size),\n            usage: UsageIndex::new(block_size),\n            header: Header::default(),\n            free_set: BTreeSet::new(),\n            ram: [BTreeSet::new(), BTreeSet::new()],\n        };\n        links.sync_header();\n        links\n    }\n\n    /// Rebuilds the in-memory state of loaded records.\n    pub fn from_parts(records: Records, usage: UsageIndex, header: Header) -> Result<Self> {\n        let mut links = Self {\n            records,\n            usage,\n            header,\n            free_set: BTreeSet::new(),\n            ram: [BTreeSet::new(), BTreeSet::new()],\n        };\n        if header.allocated >= links.records.capacity().max(1) && header.allocated != 0 {\n            return Err(Error::corrupt(\"links header exceeds the records\"));\n        }\n        if links.records.layout != Layout::United {\n            for index in 1..=header.allocated {\n     return;\n        }\n        for index in 1..=self.header.allocated {\n            if self.exists(index) {\n                self.ram_update(index, true);\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn ram_wants(&self, end: u64) -> bool {\n        self.records.layout == Layout::DataOnly && (!self.usage.enabled() || !is_internal(end))\n    }\n\n    fn ram_update(&mut self, index: u64, insert: bool) {\n        for role in ROLES {\n            let end = self.records.end(index, role);\n            if self.ram_wants(end) {\n                let key = (end, self.records.other_end(index, role), index);\n                let set = &mut self.ram[role_index(role)];\n                if insert {\n                    set.insert(key);\n                } else {\n                    set.remove(&key);\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// The layout.\n    #[must_use]\n    pub const fn layout(&self) -> Layout {\n        self.records.layout\n    }\n\n    /// The header.\n    #[must_use]\n    pub const fn header(&self) -> Header {\n        self.header\n    }\n\n    /// Highest allocated index.\n    #[must_use]\n    pub const fn allocated(&self) -> u64 {\n        self.header.allocated\n    }\n\n    /// Number of live links.\n    #[must_use]\n    pub const fn count(&self) -> u64 {\n        self.header.allocated - self.header.free\n    }\n\n    /// Mirrors the header into the records (doublets-compatible header).\n    pub fn sync_header(&mut self) {\n        let h = self.header;\n        if self.records.layout == Layout::DataOnly {\n            return;\n        }\n        self.records.ensure(h.allocated);\n        let reserved = self.records.capacity().saturating_sub(1);\n        for (cell, value) in [\n            (header::ALLOCATED, h.allocated),\n            (header::RESERVED, reserved),\n            (header::FREE, h.free),\n            (header::FIRST_FREE, h.first_free),\n            (header::ROOT_AS_SOURCE, h.root_as_source),\n            (header::ROOT_AS_TARGET, h.root_as_target),\n            (header::LAST_FREE, h.last_free),\n        ] {\n            self.records.set_header(cell, value);\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn united_unused(&self, index: u64) -> bool {\n        if index <= self.header.allocated && self.header.first_free != index {\n            self.records.tree_cell(index, Role::Source, 2) == 0 && self.records.source(index) != 0\n        } else {\n            true\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Whether `index` is a live link.\n    #[must_use]\n    pub fn exists(&self, index: u64) -> bool {\n        if index == 0 || index > self.header.allocated {\n            return false;\n        }\n        match self.records.layout {\n            Layout::United => !self.united_unused(index),\n            _ => self.records.source(index) != 0 || self.records.target(index) != 0,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Reads a live link.\n    pub fn get(&self, index: u64) -> Result<Link> {\n        if !self.exists(index) {\n            return Err(Error::NotFound);\n        }\n        Ok(Link { index, source: self.records.source(index), target: self.records.target(index) })\n    }\n\n    /// Source 0\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Target of a live link (0 if missing).\n    #[must_use]\n    pub fn target(&self, index: u64) -> u64 {\n        if self.exists(index) {\n            self.records.target(index)\n        } else {\n            0\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn check_ref(&self, raw: u64, own: u64) -> Result<()> {\n        if is_internal(raw) && raw != own && !self.exists(raw) {\n            return Err(Error::invalid(format!(\"link {raw} does not exist\")));\n        }\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// Creates `source -> target`; fails with [`Error::Exists`] for duplicates.\n    pub fn create(&mut self, source: u64, target: u64) -> Result<u64> {\n        if source == 0 && target == 0 {\n            return Err(Error::invalid(\"a link self.sync_header();\n        Ok(index)\n    }\n\n    /// Finds `source -> target` or creates it.\n    pub fn get_or_create(&mut self, source: u64, target: u64) -> Result<u64> {\n        match self.search(source, target) {\n            Some(index) => Ok(index),\n            None => self.create(source, target),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Changes both ends of a live link.\n    pub fn     }\n        if source == 0 && target == 0 {\n            return Err(Error::invalid(\"a link needs a non-null end\"));\n        }\n        self.check_ref(source, index)?;\n        self.check_ref(target, index)?;\n        if self.search(source, target).is_some() {\n            return Err(Error::Exists);\n        }\n        self.detach(index)?;\n        self.attach(index, source, target)?;\n        self.sync_header();\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// Number of other links that refer to `index`.\n    #[must_use]\n    pub fn references(&self, index: u64) -> u64 {\n        let mut count = self.count_role(Role::Source, index) + self.count_role(Role::Target, index);\n        if self.exists(index) {\n            count -= u64::from(self.records.source(index) == index) + u64::from(self.records.target(index) == index);\n        }\n        count\n    }\n\n    /// Deletes a link that no other link refers to.\n    pub fn delete(&mut self, index: u64) -> Result<()> {\n        self.get(index)?;\n        let refs = self.references(index);\n        if refs > 0 {\n            return Err(Error::Busy(format!(\"link {index} is referenced by {refs} links\")));\n        }\n        self.detach(index)?;\n        self.free_slot(index);\n        self.sync_header();\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    fn allocate_slot(&mut self) -> u64 {\n        let index = match self.records.layout {\n            Layout::United if self.header.first_free != 0 => {\n                let index = self.header.first_free;\n                self.free_list_detach(index);\n                index\n            }\n            Layout::Split | Layout::DataOnly if !self.free_set.is_empty() => {\n                let index = self.free_set.pop_first().unwrap_or_default();\n                self.header.free -= 1;\n                index\n            }\n            _ => {\n                self.header.allocated += 1;\n                self.header.allocated\n            }\n        };\n        self.records.ensure(index);\n        self.records.set_link(index, 0, 0);\n        if self.records.layout.has_embedded_index() {\n            for role in ROLES {\n                for which in 0..3 {\n                    self.records.set_tree_cell(index, role, which, 0);\n                }\n            }\n        }\n        index\n    }\n\n    fn free_slot(&mut self, index: u64) {\n        if index < self.header.allocated {\n            if self.records.layout == Layout::United {\n                self.free_list_attach_first(index);\n            } else {\n                self.free_set.insert(index);\n                self.header.free += 1;\n            }\n            return;\n        }\n        self.header.allocated -= 1;\n        loop {\n            let top = self.header.allocated;\n            if top == 0 {\n                break;\n            }\n            if self.records.layout == Layout::United {\n                if !self.united_unused(top) {\n                    break;\n                }\n                self.free_list_detach(top);\n            } else {\n                if !self.free_set.remove(&top) {\n                    break;\n                }\n                self.header.free -= 1;\n            }\n            self.header.allocated -= 1;\n        }\n    }\n\n    // The doublets unused-links list: an absolute circular doubly linked\n    // list with `previous = source` and `next = target`.\n    fn free_list_attach_first(&mut self, element: u64) {\n        let first = self.header.first_free;\n        if first == 0 {\n            self.header.first_free = element;\n            self.header.last_free = element;\n            self.records.set_link(element, element, element);\n        } else {\n            let previous = self.records.source(first);\n            self.records.set_link(element, previous, first);\n            let previous_source = self.records.source(previous);\n            self.records.set_link(previous, previous_source, element);\n            let first_target = self.records.target(first);\n            self.records.set_link(first, element, first_target);\n            self.header.first_free = element;\n        }\n        self.header.free += 1;\n    }\n\n    fn free_list_detach(&mut self, element: u64) {\n        let previous = self.records.source(element);\n        let next = self.records.target(element);\n        if next == element {\n            self.header.first_free = 0;\n            self.header.last_free = 0;\n        } else {\n            let previous_source = self.records.source(previous);\n            self.records.set_link(previous, previous_source, next);\n            let next_target = self.records.target(next);\n            self.records.set_link(next, previous, next_target);\n            if element == self.header.first_free {\n                self.header.first_free = next;\n            }\n            if element == self.header.last_free {\n                self.header.last_free = previous;\n            }\n        }\n        self.records.set_link(element, 0, 0);\n        self.header.free -= 1;\n    }\n\n    fn tree_root(&self, tree: TreeId, role:        (TreeId::PerLink(link), role) => self.records.link_root(link, role),\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn set_tree_root(&mut self, tree: TreeId, role: Role, root: u64) {\n        match (tree, role) {\n target);\n        for role in ROLES {\n            if let Some(tree) = self.records.tree_of(index, role) {\n                let root = self.tree_root(tree, role);\n                let per_link =      self.set_tree_root(tree, role, root);\n            }\n            self.usage.add(&self.records, index, role, self.header.allocated)?;\n        }\n        self.ram_update(index, true);\n self.header.allocated)?;\n            if let Some(tree) = self.records.tree_of(index, role) {\n                let root = self.tree_root(tree, role);\n                let per_link = matches!(tree, TreeId::PerLink(_));\n                let mut view = TreeMut { records: &mut self.records, role, per_link };\n                let key = view.key(index);\n                let root = sbt::remove(&mut TreeId, role: Role) -> (Tree<'_>, u64) {\n        let per_link = matches!(tree, TreeId::PerLink(_));\n        (Tree { records: &self.records, role, per_link }, self.tree_root(tree, role))\n    }\n\n    /// The tree holding links whose `role` end is `end`.\n    fn tree_for(&self, role: Role, end: u64) -> Option<TreeId> {\n        match self.records.layout {\n            Layout::United if end != 0 => Some(TreeId::Global),\n            Layout::Split if is_internal(end) => {\n                if self.exists(end) {\n                    Some(TreeId::PerLink(end))\n                } else {\n                    None\n                }\n            }\n            Layout::Split if end != 0 => Some(TreeId::Global),\n            _ => {\n                let _ = role;\n                None\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn uses_usage(&self, end: u64) -> bool {\n        self.records.layout == Layout::DataOnly && self.usage.enabled() && is_internal(end)\n    }\n\n    /// Finds the link `source -> target`.\n    #[must_use]\n    pub fn search(&self, source: u64, target: u64) -> Option<u64> {\n        match self.records.layout {\n            Layout::DataOnly => {\n                if self.uses_usage(source) {\n                    self.usage.find(&self.records, source, Role::Source, target)\n                } else if self.uses_usage(target) {\n                    self.usage.find(&self.records, target, Role::Target, source)\n                } else {\n                    let low = (source, target, 0);\n                    self.ram[0].range(low..=(source, target,                  (Role::Source, source, target)\n                } else {\n                    (Role::Target, target, source)\n                };\n                if is_internal(end) &&      });\n                        found\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Visits the links whose `role` end is `end`; returns `false` if stopped.\n    pub fn each_role(&self, role: Role, end: u64, visit: &mut dyn FnMut(u64) -> bool) -> bool {\n        if self.uses_usage(end) {\n            return self.usage.each(&self.records, end, role, visit);\n        }\n        if self.records.layout == Layout::DataOnly {\n            let set = &self.ram[role_index(role)];\n            return set.range((end, 0, 0)..=(end, u64::MAX, u64::MAX)).all(|key|  }\n    }\n\n    /// Visits every live link in index order; returns `false` if stopped.\n    pub fn each_link(&self, visit: &mut dyn FnMut(Link) -> bool) -> bool {\n        for index in          return false;\n            }\n        }\n        true\n    }\n\n    /// All live links.\n    #[must_use]\n    pub fn all(&self) -> Vec<Link> {\n        let mut out =   && (self.usage.threshold - threshold).abs() < f64::EPSILON\n            && (self.usage.hysteresis - hysteresis).abs() < f64::EPSILON;\n        if unchanged {\n            return Ok(());\n        }\n        self.usage.var.clear(space);\n        self.usage.handles.truncate_chunks(0, space);\n        self.usage.mode = mode;\n        self.usage.threshold = threshold;\n        self.usage.hysteresis =  /// Releases record chunks above `allocated`.\n    pub fn shrink(&mut self, space: &mut Space) {\n        let keep = self.header.allocated + 1;\n        self.records.data.truncate_chunks(keep, space);\n        if self.records.layout == Layout::Split {\n            self.records.index.truncate_chunks(keep, space);\n        }\n        self.usage.handles.truncate_chunks(keep, space);\n        self.usage.var.shrink(space);\n        self.sync_header();\n    }\n\n    /// Verifies every invariant; returns a list of problems.\n    #[must_use]\n    pub fn check(&self) -> Vec<String> {\n        let mut problems = Vec::new();\n        let mut live = 0;\n        for link in self.all() {\n            live += 1;\n            for (raw, what) in [(link.source, \"source\"), (link.target, \"target\")] {\n                if is_internal(raw) && !self.exists(raw) {\n                    problems.push(format!(\"link {} has a dangling {what} {raw}\", link.index));\n                }\n            }\n            if self.search(link.source, link.target) != Some(link.index) {\n                problems.push(format!(\"link {} is not found by its ends\", link.index));\n            }\n        }\n Metadata tx including the superblock → checkpoint → `space.commit()`.\n     - Journal off: checkpoint directly.\n   - **Planned FS schema:**\n     - Type points: 1..5 are markers, 6 FILE, 7 DIR, 8 SYMLINK.\n     - Inode link I = (TYPE, ext(slot)), ino = slot+1, root is slot 0.\n     - Name N = (3, chain); chain cells are (ext(cp), rest) ending in (ext(cn), 0). Packed encoding: ext(len<<56 | ≤7 bytes).\n     - Entry E = (dir, N); binding B = (E, child); symlink S = (I, N_target). Names are unique per directory automatically.\n     - nlink = number of B links targeting I. Parent found via target=D → B → source(source(B)).\n     - Inode record of 64 B: mode u32 (0 = free), nlink u32, uid u32, gid u32, size u64, start u64, blocks u64, mtime/ctime/atime i64.\n     - One contiguous extent per file. Growth order: in place with growth% → exact in place → evict movable chunks → relocate the file → compact → ENOSPC.\n     - Zero-fill newly exposed ranges.\n     - Data writes: fresh blocks go direct. Live blocks go direct in metadata mode, or to a cache journaled at commit in full mode. Drop cache entries when a range is freed.\n     - Trim slack on release.\n     - Virtual `/.lfs/` directory: config, map.json, links, stats.\n   - **Toolchain and CI:**\n     - Local toolchain is rustc 1.99, rust-version 1.87.\n     - clippy pedantic+nursery with -Dwarnings in CI (`cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features`); `cargo fmt --all -- --check`; `cargo doc --no-deps --all-features`.\n     - `unsafe_code` forbidden; max 1000 lines per file.\n\n3. On mount it is\n//! replayed if it is valid and its sequence number is the superblock's plus\n//! one (or the superblock is torn and the transaction carries block 0).\n//! LEB128     N                 number of links, each `source target`\n//!\n//! explicit layout (bit 1 set):\n//! LEB128     S                 number of sections, then S section headers:\n//! LEB128     shape             bits 0-1  log2 of the reference width in bytes\n//!                              bit 2     a gap follows\n//!                              bit 3     variable arity (else every link\n//!                                        holds exactly min_arity references)\n//!                              bits 4+   min_arity, at least 1\n//! LEB128     gap               addresses skipped before the section (if bit 2)\n//! LEB128     extra_arity       0 = no maximum, else max - min (if bit 3)\n//! LEB128     count             number of links in the section\n//!\n//! links, section by section; a link in a variable-arity section starts\n//! with LEB128 (length - min_arity); every reference is `width` bytes,\n//! little-endian\n//! ```\n//!\n//! Address `0` is null. The first section starts at `1 + gap` and every\n//! other section at `previous end + gap`, so gaps leave holes. The compact\n//! layout is exactly one section with gap 5 (the LiNo marker points\n//! `1..=5`), arity 2 and the header width.\n//!\n//! Each section has its own width: the narrowest of 1, 2, 4 and 8 bytes\n//! that holds every reference in it, so links that only refer to small\n//! addresses stay small wherever they live. [`LinksPacket::pack`] chooses\n//! the sections.\n//!\n//! With external references enabled the top bit of a reference marks it as\n//! external, exactly like `Platform.Data.Hybrid<T>`: value `v ≥ 1` is stored as\n//! the two's-complement negation `2^bits - v` and value `0` as `2^(bits-1)`.\n//! SHAPE_VARIABLE_ARITY: u64 = 0b1000;\nconst SHAPE_MIN_ARITY_SHIFT: u32 = 4;\n\n/// Null link address.\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// Reads a section header, returning the still empty section and SHAPE_VARIABLE_ARITY != 0 {\n            Some(read_leb128(reader)?)\n        } else {\n            None\n        };\n        let arity = ArityRange::from_shape(shape >> SHAPE_MIN_ARITY_SHIFT, extra)?;\n        let count = read_leb128(reader)?;\n        let section = Section {\n            gap,\n            arity,\n            width,\n            links: Vec::new(),\n        };\n Helpers: `external(v)`, `as_external(raw)`, `is_external`, `is_internal`.\n   - **Usage index** (`UsageIndex {handles: ChunkedArray(16), var: VarStore, mode, threshold, hysteresis}`): adaptive tree/bitstring. `Links::set_index(mode, threshold, hysteresis, &mut space)` rebuilds it.\n   - **Space allocator** (`Space`):\n     - Methods: new(total), mark_used, allocate(len, Fit), allocate_avoiding, allocate_at, free (fresh blocks free immediately, committed ones pend until commit), commit, is_fresh, is_free, free_extents, largest_free, free_blocks.\n     - `Fit::{Best, First}`.\n   - **ChunkedArray**:\n     - Methods: new(record_size, bs), ensure_capacity, truncate_chunks, record/record_mut/get/set, place(space, fit), take_writes(&mut Vec<BlockWrite>), relocate(index, space, fit, avoid), relocate_table, chunk_at(block) (exact start only), chunk_blocks_iter, table_extent, live_dirty_blocks(space), cow_live(space, fit, with_table), is_dirty, mark_all_dirty, descriptor, load(device, desc, record_size, bs, space).\n     - `BlockWrite = (u64, Vec<u8>)`.\n   - **Journal**:\n     - `Journal {start, blocks, block_size}` with default_blocks(total), exists (≥3 blocks), capacity, commit(device, seq, writes) (syncs twice), read(device) -> Option<Transaction{seq, writes}>, wipe.\n     - Free function `checkpoint(device, writes)` writes block 0 last, after a sync.\n     - Replay iff tx.seq == sb.seq+1, or the superblock is torn and the tx touches block 0.\n   - **Device:** `BlockDevice` trait (len_bytes, read_at, write_at with byte offsets, sync). Implementations: MemDevice, FileDevice, CrashDevice (write budget; `image()`).\n   - **Config:**\n     - `RuntimeConfig` fields: journal Off/Metadata/Full, commit_every, alloc Fit, gap_fill, growth_percent, index IndexMode, bitstring_threshold Threshold, hysteresis_percent, auto_compact, atime, read_only, protect_structure.\n     - Methods: set, set_assignment, apply_lino, pairs, to_lino, chunk_fit.\n     - `FormatOptions {block_size, layout, name_encoding, journal_blocks: Option<u64>}`.\n     - `Layout::{United, Split, DataOnly}`; `NameEncoding::{Chars, Packed}`.\n   - **Error variants:** Io, Corrupt, NotFound, Exists, NotDir, IsDir, NotEmpty, NoSpace, InvalidArgument, Unsupported, NameTooLong, ReadOnly, Busy. Constructors `Error::corrupt()` and `Error::invalid()`; `errno()`.\n   - **Planned FS schema:**\n     - Links 1..5 are LiNo marker points created at format: ONE, NUMBER, STRING = 3, LIST, IDENTIFIED. Then 6 FILE, 7 DIR, 8 SYMLINK, 9 CONFIG; TYPE_POINTS = 9.\n     - Inode link I = (TYPE, ext(slot)); ino = slot+1; root is slot 0 (ROOT_INO = 1).\n     - Name N = string link (STRING, chain). Entry E = (I_dir, N). Binding B = (E, I_child). Symlink S = (I_symlink, N_target). Config C = (CONFIG, string of config lino text); sb.config = C.\n     - Parent found via each_target(I) → B → source(source(B)).\n     - nlink: files count their bindings; dirs are 2 + subdirs.\n   - **Planned commit:**\n     1. sync_header.\n     2. Place all arrays with chunk_fit.\n     3. If journaling (journal exists, mode != Off, sb.seq > 0) and live dirty + 1 > capacity, run cow_live without tables; if still over, with tables; if still over, error.\n     4. Encode the superblock with seq+1 (header, descriptors).\n     5. take_writes from all arrays. Write fresh blocks directly and sync.\n     6. Full-mode data cache: include it in the metadata tx if it fits; otherwise commit it in pieces as txs with seq+1 and no block 0, checkpointing each piece.\n     7. Metadata tx plus superblock → journal.commit → checkpoint.\n     8. Journal off: wipe the journal once (`journal_wiped` flag), then checkpoint everything with the superblock last.\n     9. seq += 1, space.commit(), clear dirty and ops.\n   - **Planned open:**\n     - Read 1024 bytes, peek_block_size, decode.\n     - If the superblock is torn, try block sizes 1024..65536 with journal start fixed at 1 and replay a tx that touches block 0.\n     - Replay is allowed only when the device is writable; otherwise return Unsupported.\n     - Load the space (superblock, journal, arrays: links data at record size 64 for united else 16; index 64; usage 16; var via VarStore::load; inodes 64).\n     - Links::from_parts with usage mode/threshold/hysteresis taken from the superblock.\n     - Read config from the C link; if the index config differs, run set_index.\n     - Clean up orphans (mode != 0, nlink == 0); mark file extents used.\n   - **Planned file data:**\n     - One contiguous extent per file.\n     - Growth order: in place with growth% → exact in place → evict chunks (needs a new `chunk_covering(block)` helper; commit if the freed blocks are pending) → relocate the file (copy) → compact if auto_compact → ENOSPC.\n     - Direct device writes for fresh blocks and in Off/Metadata modes. In Full mode, live blocks go to a `cache: BTreeMap<u64, Vec<u8>>`; reads consult the cache. Drop cache entries when a range is freed.\n     - Zero-fill [old_size, new_size) on extension. Trim slack on release.\n     - Open counts are tracked in RAM to defer freeing unlinked files.\n   - **Planned compaction:** commit, then passes that move each owner (file, chunk, table) into the lowest free extent that fits and lies before it, committing between passes. Trim slack first.\n   - **Planned virtual `/.lfs`:** a control dir with config (rw, applied on flush/release), map.json, links, stats. Virtual inos sit near u64::MAX, e.g. CONTROL_DIR_INO = 0xFFFF_FFFF_FFFF_FF00 with files at +1..+4. \".lfs\" is reserved in the root.\n   - **Planned links DB API:** create/update/delete/search with protect_structure. Refuse creating links whose source is a type point, an inode link or an entry. Refuse updating or deleting structural links, or referenced links.\n   - **Toolchain and CI:** clippy pedantic+nursery `-Dwarnings`, `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo doc`, `unsafe_code` forbidden, max 1000 lines per file. `src/main.rs` is `fn main() {}` (one const-fn warning until the CLI replaces it).\n\n3. [2026-10-21T21:55:21.694Z] [INFO]     "originalFile": "//! Relocatable arrays of fixed-size records.\n//!\n//! Links, inodes, usage handles and every size class of the variable-size\n//! store are [`ChunkedArray`]s: records live in small chunks (one block, or\n//! one record when records are larger than a block) that can sit anywhere on\n//! the device. Chunks are what fills the gaps between contiguous files, and\n//! they are \"liquid\": the allocator may move a chunk to let a file grow in\n//! place. A chunk table (one `u64` block number per chunk) stored in its own\n//! contiguous extent locates the chunks.\n//!\n//! New chunks get their blocks only at commit (delayed allocation), so the\n//! allocator sees the final set of new chunks at once and places each of\n//! them in the smallest gap.\n\nuse crate::codec::{get_u64, put_u64};\nuse crate::device::BlockDevice;\nuse crate::error::{Error, Result};\nuse crate::space::{Fit, Space};\n\n/// Block number of a chunk that has not been placed yet.\npub const UNPLACED: u64 = u64::MAX;\n\n/// Where a chunk table lives on disk.\n#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct ArrayDescriptor {\n    /// First block of the chunk table extent.\n    pub table_start: u64,\n    /// Blocks reserved for the chunk table.\n    pub table_blocks: u64,\n    /// Number of chunks in use.\n    pub chunks: u64,\n}\n\nimpl ArrayDescriptor {\n    /// Encoded size in bytes.\n    pub const SIZE: usize = 24;\n\n    /// Encodes the descriptor.\n    pub fn write(&self, bytes: &mut [u8]) {\n        put_u64(bytes, 0, self.table_start);\n        put_u64(bytes, 8, self.table_blocks);\n        put_u64(bytes, 16, self.chunks);\n    }\n\n    /// Decodes a descriptor.\n    #[must_use]\n    pub fn read(bytes: &[u8]) -> Self {\n        Self {\n            table_start: get_u64(bytes, 0),\n            table_blocks: get_u64(bytes, 8),\n            chunks: get_u64(bytes, 16),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n#[derive(Clone, Debug)]\nstruct Chunk {\n    block: u64,\n    data: Vec<u8>,\n    dirty: bool,\n}\n\n/// A growable array of `record_size`-byte records stored in relocatable chunks.\n#[derive(Clone, Debug)]\npub struct ChunkedArray {\n    record_size: usize,\n    block_size: usize,\n    chunk_blocks: u64,\n    per_chunk: usize,\n    chunks: Vec<Chunk>,\n    table_start: u64,\n    table_blocks: u64,\n    table_dirty: bool,\n}\n\n/// One block that must be written at commit.\npub type BlockWrite = (u64, Vec<u8>);\n\nimpl ChunkedArray {\n    /// An empty array.\n    #[must_use]\n    pub fn new(record_size: usize, block_size: usize) -> Self {\n        let chunk_bytes = record_size.max(block_size);\n        let chunk_blocks = chunk_bytes.div_ceil(block_size) as u64;\n        Self {\n volume, crashing after every possible number\n/// of device writes; each surviving image must mount cleanly and show\n/// either the state before or after the step.\nfn crash_everywhere(\n    journal: &str,\n    setup: impl Fn(&mut Fs<CrashDevice>),\n    step: impl Fn(&mut Fs<CrashDevice>),\n    verify: impl Fn(&mut Fs<MemDevice>) -> bool,\n    verify_old: impl Fn(&mut Fs<MemDevice>) -> bool,\n) {\n    let device = CrashDevice::new(vec![0; MIB as usize], None);\n    let mut fs = Fs::format(device, &options(1024, Layout::United), \"crash\").unwrap();\n    fs.set_config_value(\"journal\", journal).unwrap();\n    fs.set_config_value(\"commit-every\", \"0\").unwrap();\n    setup(&mut fs);\n    fs.commit().unwrap();\n    let base = fs.into_device().image();\n    // Count the writes of the step.\n    let mut probe = Fs::open(CrashDevice::new(base.clone(), None), true, &[]).unwrap();\n    step(&mut probe);\n    probe.commit().unwrap();\n    let writes = probe.into_device().writes_done();\n    assert!(writes > 0);\n    let (mut old, mut new) = (0, 0);\n    for budget in 0..=writes {\n        let mut fs = Fs::open(CrashDevice::new(base.clone(), Some(budget)), true, &[]).unwrap();\n        step(&mut fs);\n        let _ = fs.commit();\n        let image = fs.into_device().image();\n        let mut fs = Fs::open(MemDevice::from_bytes(image), true, &[])\n            .unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!(\"{journal}: crash after {budget} writes: {error}\"));\n        let problems = fs.check();\n        assert!(problems.is_empty(), \"{journal}: crash after {budget} writes: {problems:#?}\");\n        if verify(&mut fs) {\n            new += 1;\n        } else {\n            assert!(verify_old(&mut fs), \"{journal}: crash after {budget} writes: mixed state\");\n            old += 1;\n        }\n    }\n    assert!(old > 0 && new > 0);\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn crashes_never_corrupt_metadata() {\n    for journal in [\"metadata\", \"full\", [2026-10-21T22:04:22.574Z] [INFO]           "+    let mut fs = Fs::format(MemDevice::new(2 * MIB), &options(1024, Layout::United), \"g\").unwrap();",
[2026-10-21T22:04:22.574Z] [INFO]           "+    let mut inos = Vec::new();",
[2026-10-21T22:04:22.574Z] [INFO]           "+    for i in 0..8 {",
[2026-10-21T22:04:22.574Z] [INFO]           "+        inos.push(put(&mut fs, &format!(\"/f{i}\"), &pattern(3000, i)));",
[2026-10-21T22:04:22.574Z] [INFO]           "+    }",
[2026-10-21T22:04:22.574Z] [INFO]           "+    // Grow every file in small appends so neighbours block each other.",
[2026-10-21T22:04:22.574Z] [INFO]           "+    let mut expected: Vec<Vec<u8>> = (0..8).map(|i| pattern(3000, i)).collect();",
[2026-10-21T22:04:22.574Z] [INFO]           "+    for round in 0..30u8 {",
[2026-10-21T22:04:22.574Z] [INFO]           "+        for (i, &ino) in inos.iter().enumerate() {",
[2026-10-21T22:04:22.574Z] [INFO]           "+            let chunk = pattern(700, round ^ i as u8);",
[2026-10-21T22:04:22.574Z] [INFO]           "+            let offset = expected[i].len() as u64;",
[2026-10-21T22:04:22.574Z] [INFO]           "+            fs.write(ino, offset, &chunk).unwrap();",
[2026-10-21T22:04:22.574Z] [INFO]           "+            expected[i].extend_from_slice(&chunk);",
[2026-10-21T22:04:22.574Z] [INFO]           "+        }",
[2026-10-21T22:04:22.574Z] [INFO]           "+        // Names add links, which take blocks between files.",
[2026-10-21T22:04:22.574Z] [INFO]           "+        put(&mut fs, &format!(\"/n{round}\"), b\"\");",
[2026-10-21T22:04:22.574Z] [INFO]           "+    }",

[2026-10-21T22:04:22.574Z] [INFO]           "+",
[2026-10-21T22:04:22.574Z] [INFO]           "+/// Runs `step` on a committed volume, crashing after every possible number",
[2026-10-21T22:04:22.574Z] [INFO]           "+/// of device writes; each surviving image must mount cleanly and show",
[2026-10-21T22:04:22.574Z] [INFO]           "+/// either the state before or after the step.",
[2026-10-21T22:04:22.574Z] [INFO]           "+fn crash_everywhere(",
[2026-10-21T22:04:22.574Z] [INFO]           "+    journal: &str,",
[2026-10-21T22:04:22.574Z] [INFO]           "+    setup: impl Fn(&mut Fs<CrashDevice>),",
[2026-10-21T22:04:22.574Z] [INFO]           "+    step: impl Fn(&mut Fs<CrashDevice>),",
[2026-10-21T22:04:22.574Z] [INFO]           "+    verify: impl Fn(&mut Fs<MemDevice>) -> bool,",
[2026-10-21T22:04:22.574Z] [INFO]           "+    verify_old: impl Fn(&mut Fs<MemDevice>) -> bool,",
[2026-10-21T22:04:22.574Z] [INFO]           "+) {",
[2026-10-21T22:04:22.574Z] [INFO]           "+    let device = CrashDevice::new(vec![0; MIB as usize], None);",
[2026-10-21T22:04:22.574Z] [INFO]           "+    let mut fs = Fs::format(device, &options(1024, Layout::United), \"crash\").unwrap();",
[2026-10-21T22:04:22.574Z] [INFO]           "+    fs.set_config_value(\"journal\", journal).unwrap();",
[2026-10-21T22:04:22.574Z] [INFO]           "+    fs.set_config_value(\"commit-every\", \"0\").unwrap();",
[2026-10-21T22:04:22.574Z] [INFO]           "+    setup(&mut fs);",
[2026-10-21T22:04:22.574Z] [INFO]           "+    fs.commit().unwrap();",
[2026-10-21T22:04:22.574Z] [INFO]           "+    let base = fs.into_device().image();",
[2026-10-21T22:04:22.574Z] [INFO]           "+    // Count the writes of the step.",
[2026-10-21T22:04:22.574Z] [INFO]           "+    let mut probe = Fs::open(CrashDevice::new(base.clone(), None), true, &[]).unwrap();",
[2026-10-21T22:04:22.574Z] [INFO]           "+    step(&mut probe);",
[2026-10-21T22:04:22.574Z] [INFO]           "+    probe.commit().unwrap();",
[2026-10-21T22:04:22.574Z] [INFO]           "+    let writes = probe.into_device().writes_done();",
[2026-10-21T22:04:22.574Z] [INFO]           "+    assert!(writes > 0);",

components(links: &[Link], position: &HashMap<u64, usize>) -> Vec<Vec<usize>> {\n    const NONE: usize = usize::MAX;\n    let deps = |node: usize| {\n        let link = links[node];\n        [link.source, link.target]\n            .into_iter()\n            .filter_map(|end| position.get(&end).copied())\n    };\n    let count = links.len();\n    let (mut index, mut low) = (vec![NONE; count], vec![0; count]);\n    let mut on_stack = vec![false; count];\n    let (mut stack, mut out, mut next) = (Vec::new(), Vec::new(), 0);\n    for root in 0..count {\n        if index[root] != NONE {\n            continue;\n        }\n        let mut work = vec![(root, 0)];\n        while let Some((node, edge)) = work.pop() {\n            if edge == 0 {\n                index[node] = next;\n                low[node] = next;\n                next += 1;\n                stack.push(node);\n                on_stack[node] = true;\n            }\n            if let Some(dep) = deps(node).nth(edge) {\n                work.push((node, edge + 1));\n                if index[dep] == NONE {\n                    work.push((dep, 0));\n                } else if on_stack[dep] {\n                    low[node] = low[node].min(index[dep]);\n                }\n                continue;\n            }\n            if let Some(&(parent, _)) = work.last() {\n                low[parent] = low[parent].min(low[node]);\n            }\n            if low[node] == index[node] {\n                let mut component = Vec::new();\n                while let Some(member) = stack.pop() {\n                    on_stack[member] = false;\n                    component.push(member);\n                    if member == node {\n                        break;\n                    }\n                }\n                out.push(component);\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    out\n}\n\n/// Imports links under new addresses and returns the map from the old\n/// addresses to the new ones.\n///\n/// Every A link that does not\n/// refer to itself, directly or through a cycle, is looked up first and only\n/// created if missing, so importing the same links twice adds nothing.\n/// Points and cycles are created anew at fresh addresses. Nothing changes\n/// if a check fails.\npub fn import_remapped(store: &mut Links, links: &[Link]) -> Result<HashMap<u64, u64>> {\n    let position: HashMap<u64, usize> = links\n        .iter()\n        .enumerate()\n        .map(|(position, link)| (link.index, position))\n        .collect();\n    if position.len() != links.len() {\n        return Err(Error::invalid(\"a link index appears {\n        if is_internal(end) {\n            map.get(&end).copied().unwrap_or(end)\n        } else {\n            end\n        }\n    };\n    for component in components(links, &position) {\n (translate(&map, link.source), translate(&map, link.target));\n            map.insert(link.index, store.get_or_create(source, target)?);\n            continue;\n        }\n        let mut next = store.allocated();\n        for &member in &component {\n            next += 1;\n            map.insert(links[member].index, next);\n        }\n        let mut placed: Vec<Link> = component\n            .iter()\n            .map(|&member| {\n                let link = links[member];\n                Link {\n                    index: map[&link.index],\n                    source: translate(&map, components(links: &[Link], position: &HashMap<u64, usize>) -> Vec<Vec<usize>> {\n    const NONE: usize = usize::MAX;\n    let deps = |node: usize| {\n        let link = links[node];\n  .enumerate()\n        .map(|(position, link)| (link.index, position))\n        .collect();\n    if position.len() != links.len() {\n        return Err(Error::invalid(\"a link index appears link.source),\n                    target: translate(&map, link.target),\n                }\n            })\n            .collect();\n        placed.sort_unstable_by_key(|link| link.index);\n
