Finally it calls sync_header.\n   - **src/links/packet.rs** (new, about 420 lines). Module docs describe the three formats.\n     - `pub const DOUBLETS_RECORD: usize = 64;`\n     - `pub enum Format {Archive, Doublets, Lino}`: ALL; `name()` gives \"binary\" / \"doublets\" / \"lino\"; `parse()`; `detect(bytes)` checks text first (UTF-8 starting with '(' / '#' / a digit), then whether read_archive succeeds, else Doublets; `of_path()` maps .links → Doublets, .lino/.txt → Lino, .lnb/.bin → Archive.\n     - `pub struct Archive { links: Vec<Link>, names: Vec<(u64,String)> }` with Default.\n     - `write_archive(links, names) -> Result<Vec<u8>>` packs Internal(source/target) with ext=false, packed=true, then the names packet.\n     - `read_archive(bytes)` reads two packets with unlimited limits. It rejects a short archive, trailing bytes, non-doublets, internal refs in names, and invalid chars.\n     - `write_doublets(links)` builds a `Links::new(United, 4096)`, calls place_all, dumps `records.data.record(i)` for 0..=top, and sets the reserved bytes [8..16] = top.\n     - `read_doublets(bytes)` validates the size and the header's allocated value, and filters `index != first_free && (cell(index,4) != 0 || cell(index,0) == 0)`.\n     - `write_lino(links)` emits \"(i: s t)\" lines with format_ref. `read_lino(text)` uses parse_lino_to_links, requires an id and 2 Ref values, sorts, and rejects duplicate indices.\n     - `read(format, bytes)` and `write(format, links, names)`.\n     - `fn components(links, position)` is an iterative Tarjan that returns SCCs dependencies-first.\n     - `pub fn import_remapped(store, links) -> Result<HashMap<u64,u64>>`:\n       - validates unique indices, non-null links, no duplicate pairs, and refs within the input;\n       - acyclic singleton → `get_or_create` (dedupes);\n       - cyclic or self-ref SCC → fresh addresses `allocated+1..` via place_all.\n     - Ends with `#[cfg(test)] mod tests;`.\n   - **src/links/packet/tests.rs** (new). _>::with_constants(\n        FileMapped::from_path(path).unwrap(),\n        LinksConstants::external(),\n    )\n    .unwrap()\n}\n\n/// The doublets image of the open store at `path`.\nfn image(path: std::fs::OpenOptions::new().write(true).open(path).unwrap();\n    file.seek(SeekFrom::Start(REGION)).unwrap();\n    file.write_all(&bytes).unwrap();\n    file.sync_all().unwrap();\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn doublets_reads_and_searches_our_files() {\n    let fs = volume();\n    let path = scratch(\"ours\");\n    let all = fs.links().all();\n    let any = LinksConstants::<u64>::external().any;\n    let mut Some(link.index));\n        let by_source = all.iter().filter(|l| l.source == link.source).count();\n        let by_target = all.iter().filter(|l| l.target == link.target).count();\n let back = packet::read_doublets(&image(&path)).unwrap();\n    assert_eq!(back, store.iter().map(|link| ours(&link)).collect::<Vec<_>>());\n    assert!(back.contains(&Link {\n        index: a,\n assert_eq!(back.len(), all.len() + 1);\n    drop(store);\n    let _ = std::fs::remove_file(&path);\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn files_written_by_doublets_import_into_a_volume() {\n    let path = store.create_link(previous, external(value)).unwrap();\n    }\n    let gap = store.create_link(marker, marker).unwrap();\n    store.delete(gap).unwrap();\n    store.create_link(previous, Problem Solving:\n   - **Ideas for a robust compaction design:**\n     - Keep first-fit-lower passes until there are no moves (the original behaviour). Then resolve stuck gaps one at a time: take the lowest gap with object A right after it and len(A) > gap. Stage A in a free extent above `start+len`, commit, then move A down to first-fit (the merged gap), commit. Repeat.\n     - Or a deterministic sweep with a cursor `next`.\n     - Must guarantee termination; keep a pass cap.\n     - With the journal off, chunk copy-on-write at every commit inherently leaves holes. Options:\n       - accept \"one free extent\" only for journaled modes;\n       - make the test's verify for \"off\" check `largest_free` growth instead;\n       - have copy-on-write use `Fit::First`.\n     - Also make the crash test faster: fewer writes, e.g. fewer files, or a single journal mode for the heavy check.\n     - The bounce must only trigger when it is guaranteed to make progress; consider bouncing only into the tail extent (the last free extent) to avoid cycles between middle holes.\n   - **FUSE:** verified end to end on Linux.\n   - **Dokan:** type-checked only; CI with the MSI install was pushed (b2b8a90) and still needs checking.\n\n6. [2026-10-21T23:57:53.848Z] [INFO]         "text": "Base directory for this skill: /tmp/claude-1001/bundled-skills/2.1.306/b96129bf54b53a53d89d6aada20d2d20/dataviz\n\n# Data Visualization\n\nA chart is **read by people and executed by you**. This skill turns \"make it look\ngood\" into a procedure with checks, so the result is right by construction rather\nthan by taste.\n\n**The method here is design-system-agnostic.** Nothing in the procedure, the form\nheuristic, the six checks, or the mark specs is specific to one product. A design\nsystem supplies a small set of *parameters* (its ramps, a categorical order, a\ndiverging pair, a status palette, a texture, its surfaces, its filter components);\nthe method consumes them unchanged. A **validated default palette** is the\nreference instance, fully specified in `references/palette.md`. To target your\nbrand, read that file's structure and substitute its values - touch nothing else.\n\n> The single most important habit: **the color part is computable, so compute it.**\n> Never eyeball whether a palette is colorblind-safe - run `scripts/validate_palette.js`.\n\n## The procedure - do these in order\n\nColor comes LAST. Most bad charts pick colors first.\n\n1. **Pick the form.** What is the data's job - magnitude, identity, polarity, a\n   single headline, change-over-time? The job picks the chart type, and sometimes\n   the answer is *not a chart* (a stat tile or hero number). -> `references/choosing-a-form.md`\n2. **Assign color by the job it does.** Categorical (identity), sequential\n   (magnitude), diverging (polarity), or status (state) - each has one rule.\n   Assign categorical hues in fixed order, never cycled. -> `references/color-formula.md`\n3. **VALIDATE the palette - run the script, don't reason about Delta E.**\n   `node scripts/validate_palette.js \"<hex,hex,...>\" --mode light` (relative to\n   this skill's base directory - or load it as `<script type=\"module\">` in the\n   chart's own page, where it reads\n   `data-palette` off `<body>` and logs a `console.table` report). It returns\n   pass/fail on the lightness band, chroma floor, adjacent-pair CVD separation,\n   the normal-vision floor, and contrast. Fix anything that FAILs before continuing. Re-run for\n   `--mode dark` with that mode's surface.\n4. **Apply mark specs & spacers.** Thin marks, 4px rounded data-ends anchored to\n   the baseline, 2px lines, >=8px markers, a 2px surface gap between fills (stacked\n   segments and adjacent bars alike) and a 2px surface ring on overlapping marks,\n   selective direct labels. -> `references/marks-and-anatomy.md`\n5. **Add the hover layer - by default.** An HTML/SVG chart *is* interactive; ship\n   a crosshair+tooltip on line/area and a per-mark hover tooltip on bar/dot/cell.\n   The only form that skips it is a bare stat tile with no plot. Hit targets bigger\n   than the mark; filters in one row above the charts. -> `references/interaction.md`\n6. **Final accessibility pass.** For >= 2 series a legend is always present and <= 4\n   are also direct-labeled (a single series needs no legend box - the title names\n   it), so identity is never color-alone; a table view exists; dark mode is **selected** - its own\n   steps from the same ramps, validated against the dark surface, not an automatic\n   flip; texture is available for the CVD/print/forced-colors case.\n7. **Render it and look at it.** The validator checks color, not layout - open or\n   screenshot the output and eyeball it for label collisions, geometry, and overflow\n   before calling it done.\n\nThen check the result against **`references/anti-patterns.md`** - it is the catalog\nof what goes wrong. If your chart matches an entry, it's wrong.\n\n## Non-negotiables (true in every design system)\n\n- **Assign categorical hues in fixed order, never cycled.** A 9th series is never a\n  generated hue - it folds into \"Other,\" small multiples, or composite encoding.\n- **One axis.** Never a dual-axis chart (two y-scales). Two measures of different\n  scale -> two charts, small multiples, or indexed to a common base. *(This is the\n  #1 chart mistake - see anti-patterns.)*\n- **Color follows the entity, never its rank.** A filter that changes the series\n  count must not repaint the survivors.\n- **Sequential = one hue, light->dark. Diverging = two hues + a neutral gray\n  midpoint.** Never a rainbow; never a hue at the diverging midpoint.\n- **Run the validator before shipping any categorical palette.** CVD Delta E >= 8 is the\n  target (OKLab ×100); 6-8 is a floor that is legal ONLY with secondary encoding. A\n  normal-vision floor below 15 is a hard FAIL - full-color readers can't tell the\n  pair apart; re-step it on the adjacent pairlist (secondary encoding does not excuse\n  this one); under `--pairs all` cut series or facet instead - see check 4. A contrast WARN\n  obligates visible labels or a table view - it is not dismissable.\n- **Thin marks; a legend always present for >= 2 series (none for one), with\n  selective direct labels (never a number on every point); recessive grid/axes.**\n- **Text wears text tokens, never the series color** - values, labels, and legends\n  stay in primary/secondary/muted ink; a colored mark beside them carries identity.\n- **Status colors are reserved** (good/warning/serious/critical) and never reused\n  for \"series 4\"; they ship with an icon + label, never color alone.\n\n## Plugging in a design system\n\nThe method is invariant; only these parameters change per system. The reference\ninstance - every value filled in - is `references/palette.md`.\n\n| Parameter | What the system provides |\n|---|---|\n| **Ramps** | the hue scales (named steps) the palette draws from |\n| **Categorical theme** | the fixed hue order (a named theme); default + alternates |\n| **Sequential hue** | the default single hue for magnitude |\n| **Diverging pair** | two warm/cool poles + a neutral midpoint |\n| **Status palette** | good / warning / serious / critical - steps distinct from categorical |\n| **Texture fill** | one directional hand-drawn fill, used at 45° / 135° |\n| **Surfaces** | light & dark chart-surface colors (the validator needs these) |\n| **Filter controls** | date-range & dimension controls (behavioral spec in `interaction.md`) |\n\nTo onboard a new system: fill those rows, feed its ramps to the validator, and let\nit snap each slot to the nearest passing step. Structure and rules stay as written.\n\n## Reference files\n\n| File | What it answers |\n|------|-----------------|\n| `references/choosing-a-form.md` | Which chart type / is it even a chart? |\n| `references/color-formula.md` | The four jobs, the six checks, snap-to-passing |\n| `references/marks-and-anatomy.md` | Mark specs, spacers, labels, figures, hero number |\n| `references/interaction.md` | Tooltips & hover, filters & time ranges |\n| `references/components.md` | The pieces a chart is made of - build each in plain HTML |\n| `references/anti-patterns.md` | **What goes wrong - check every chart against this** |\n| `references/palette.md` | **The reference palette instance** - every parameter, filled in; swap for your brand's |\n| `scripts/validate_palette.js` | Runnable six-checks validator (run it; don't eyeball) |\n"

panic!(\"{path}: {error}\"))\n        .replace(\"\\r\\n\", \"\\n\")\n}\n\nfn number(map: &Value, key: &str) -> u64 {\n    map[key]\n        .as_u64()\n        .unwrap_or_else(|| panic!(\"{key} missing\"))\n}\n\n/// Checks what the page relies on: the header, and extents that cover every\n/// block once and agree with the free-space summary.\nfn check(map: &Value) {\n    assert_eq!(map[\"format\"], \"lfs-map\");\n    assert_eq!(map[\"version\"], 1);\n    let extents = map[\"extents\"].as_array().unwrap();\n    let (mut next, mut free, mut free_extents, mut largest) = (0, 0, 0, 0);\n    for extent in extents {\n        let (start, len) = (number(extent, \"start\"), number(extent, \"len\"));\n        let kind = extent[\"kind\"].as_str().unwrap();\n        assert_eq!(start, next, \"extents must be contiguous: {extent}\");\n        assert!(len > 0, \"{extent}\");\n        assert!(KINDS.contains(&kind), \"unknown kind {kind}\");\n        match kind {\n            \"free\" => {\n                free += len;\n                free_extents += 1;\n                largest = largest.max(len);\n            }\n            \"file\" => assert!(extent[\"path\"].is_string() && extent[\"ino\"].is_u64()),\n            \"chunk\" => assert!(extent[\"array\"].is_string() && extent[\"chunk\"].is_u64()),\n            \"table\" => assert!(extent[\"array\"].is_string()),\n            _ => {}\n        }\n        next = start + len;\n    }\n    assert_eq!(next, number(map, \"total_blocks\"));\n    assert_eq!(free, number(map, \"free_blocks\"));\n    assert_eq!(free_extents, number(map, \"free_extents\"));\n    assert_eq!(largest, number(map, \"largest_free\"));\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template\n\nA comprehensive template for AI-driven Rust development with full CI/CD pipeline support.\n\n[![CI/CD Pipeline](https://github.com/link-foundation/rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/workflows/CI%2FCD%20Pipeline/badge.svg)](https://github.com/link-foundation/rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/actions?workflow=CI%2FCD+Pipeline)\n[![Crates.io](https://img.shields.io/crates/v/example-sum-package-name?label=crates.io&style=flat)](https://crates.io/crates/example-sum-package-name)\n[![Docs.rs](https://img.shields.io/docsrs/example-sum-package-name?label=docs.rs&style=flat)](https://docs.rs/example-sum-package-name)\n[![Rust Version](https://img.shields.io/badge/rust-1.70%2B-blue.svg)](https://www.rust-lang.org/)\n[![Codecov](https://codecov.io/gh/link-foundation/rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/branch/main/graph/badge.svg)](https://codecov.io/gh/link-foundation/rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template)\n[![License: Unlicense](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-Unlicense-blue.svg)](http://unlicense.org/)\n\n## Features\n\n- **Rust stable support**: Works with Rust stable version\n- **Cross-platform testing**: CI runs on Ubuntu, macOS, and Windows\n- **Comprehensive testing**: Unit tests, integration tests, and doc tests\n- **Code quality**: rustfmt + Clippy with pedantic lints\n- **Pre-commit hooks**: Automated code quality checks before commits\n- **CI/CD pipeline**: GitHub Actions with multi-platform support\n- **Changelog management**: Fragment-based changelog (like Changesets/Scriv)\n- **Code coverage**: Automated coverage reports with cargo-llvm-cov and Codecov\n- **Release automation**: Automatic GitHub releases, crates.io publishing, post-publish smoke tests, and optional Docker Hub image publishing\n- **Template-safe defaults**: CI/CD skips publishing when package name is `example-sum-package-name`\n\n## Quick Start\n\n### Using This Template\n\n1. Click \"Use this template\" on GitHub to create a new repository\n2. Clone your new repository\n3. Update `Cargo.toml`:\n   - Change `name` from `example-sum-package-name` to your package name\n   - Update `description`, `repository`, and `documentation` URLs\n   - Update `[lib]` name and `[[bin]]` name\n4. Keep `Cargo.lock` committed when the project has a binary target (`[[bin]]` or `src/main.rs`)\n5. Update imports in `src/main.rs`, `tests/`, and `examples/`\n6. rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template\n\nA comprehensive template for AI-driven Rust development with full CI/CD pipeline support.\n\n[![CI/CD Pipeline](https://github.com/link-foundation/rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/workflows/CI%2FCD%20Pipeline/badge.svg)](https://github.com/link-foundation/rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/actions?workflow=CI%2FCD+Pipeline)\n[![Crates.io](https://img.shields.io/crates/v/example-sum-package-name?label=crates.io&style=flat)](https://crates.io/crates/example-sum-package-name)\n[![Docs.rs](https://img.shields.io/docsrs/example-sum-package-name?label=docs.rs&style=flat)](https://docs.rs/example-sum-package-name)\n[![Rust Version](https://img.shields.io/badge/rust-1.70%2B-blue.svg)](https://www.rust-lang.org/)\n[![Codecov](https://codecov.io/gh/link-foundation/rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/branch/main/graph/badge.svg)](https://codecov.io/gh/link-foundation/rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template)\n[![License: Unlicense](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-Unlicense-blue.svg)](http://unlicense.org/)\n\n## Features\n\n- **Rust stable support**: Works with Rust stable version\n- **Cross-platform testing**: CI runs on Ubuntu, macOS, and Windows\n- **Comprehensive testing**: Unit tests, integration tests, and doc tests\n- **Code quality**: rustfmt + Clippy with pedantic lints\n- **Pre-commit hooks**: Automated code quality checks before commits\n- **CI/CD pipeline**: GitHub Actions with multi-platform support\n- **Changelog management**: Fragment-based changelog (like Changesets/Scriv)\n- **Code coverage**: Automated coverage reports with cargo-llvm-cov and Codecov\n- **Release automation**: Automatic GitHub releases, crates.io publishing, post-publish smoke tests, and optional Docker Hub image publishing\n- **Template-safe defaults**: CI/CD skips publishing when package name is `example-sum-package-name`\n\n## Quick Start\n\n### Using This Template\n\n1. Click \"Use this template\" on GitHub to create a new repository\n2. Clone your new repository\n3. Update `Cargo.toml`:\n   - Change `name` from `example-sum-package-name` to your package name\n   - Update `description`, `repository`, and `documentation` URLs\n   - Update `[lib]` name and `[[bin]]` name\n4. Keep `Cargo.lock` committed when the project has a binary target (`[[bin]]` or `src/main.rs`)\n5. Update imports in `src/main.rs`, `tests/`, and `examples/`\n6. Demo](http://dokan-dev.github.io/images/screencast.gif)\r\n\r\n## What is Dokan\r\nWhen you want to create a new file system on Windows, other than FAT or NTFS,\r\nyou need to develop a file system driver. Developing a device driver that works\r\nin kernel mode on windows is extremely technical. By using Dokan, you can create\r\nyour own file systems very easily without writing device drivers. Dokan is\r\nsimilar to FUSE (Linux file system in user space) but works on Windows. Moreover,\r\ndokany includes a [FUSE wrapper](https://github.com/dokan-dev/dokany/wiki/FUSE)\r\nthat helps you to port your FUSE filesystems without changes.\r\n\r\n## What is Dokany\r\n*Dokany is a fork of Dokan 0.6.0 with bug fixes, clean change history and\r\nupdated to build with latest tools.*\r\n\r\nBecause the original Dokan Legacy (< 0.6.0) project is no longer maintained.\r\n\r\nSince version 0.8.0, dokany broke compatibility with the dokan API. See\r\n[Choose a version](https://github.com/dokan-dev/dokany/wiki/Installation#choose-a-version)\r\nfor more information.\r\n\r\nThe API has then again changed over time in [1.1.0](https://github.com/dokan-dev/dokany/wiki/Update-Dokan-1.0.0-application-to-Dokany-1.1.0) and [2.0.0](https://github.com/dokan-dev/dokany/wiki/Update-Dokan-1.1.0-application-to-Dokany-2.0.0).\r\n\r\n## Benchmark v1.5.1.1000 vs v2.0.3.1000\r\nA benchmark that is testing multiple scenarios repeaditly and sequentially was run 5 times against the `memfs` sample of v1.5.1.1000 and v2.0.3.1000 in an idle environment to precise results.\r\nThe detail results can be seen in this spreadsheet [here](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1zdJ6fmP_sqUGCM7SLtTle9N3JLyBOEAMRlwDLfUqm4Q/edit?usp=sharing).\r\nAs better threading and memory poll were added in v2, it is expected that concurrent scenarios (like those tests) would be even more highly improved.\r\n== /tmp/dokan-stub/dokan-sys/src/dokany/Dokan.props\n<?xml version=\"1.0\" encoding=\"utf-8\"?>\r\n<Project ToolsVersion=\"4.0\" documented in this file.\r\n\r\nThe format is based on [Keep a Changelog](http://keepachangelog.com/) and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](http://semver.org/).\r\n\r\n## [2.0.6.1000] - 2022-10-02\r\n\r\n### Changed\r\n- Library - Improve documentation.\r\n\r\n### Fixed\r\n- Kernel - Don't notify deletion on `FileDispositionInformation` completion but on `Cleanup`.\r\n\r\n## [2.0.5.1000] - 2022-07-04\r\n\r\n### Changed\r\n- FUSE - Allow override default max read size by option.\r\n- Kernel - Remove `UNCName` `CaseInSensitive` prefix during Create.\r\n- Library - Allow `FindFilesWithPattern` to return `STATUS_NOT_IMPLEMENTED` (like on v1).\r\n\r\n### Fixed\r\n- Kernel - Add `Vcb` null check before marking the volume as having wait events.\r\n- Library - Use Case sensitive option when listing filtering is done by the library.\r\n\r\n## [2.0.4.1000] - 2022-04-30\r\n\r\n### Changed\r\n- Kernel - Remove possible `UNCName` prefix in `Filename` during `CreateFile`.\r\n- Library - Doc - Recommend `FindFiles` to be implemented.\r\n- Library - Allow `FindFiles` to be optional by using `FindFilesWithPattern` with wildcard.\r\n\r\n### Fixed\r\n- Library - Move `UserContext` under `OpenCount` lock to reduce incorrect value used when calling `Close`.\r\n- Kernel - Clear write change flag when FCB is being reused.\r\n- Kernel - Remove unsupported eject media support (deadlock).\r\n- FUSE - Update library name in module definition.\r\n\r\n## [2.0.3.2000] - 2022-02-27\r\n\r\n### Fixed\r\n== Each gets the handler from `(*(*info).DokanOptions).GlobalContext as *const Handler<D>`.\n   - A `run(|| -> Result<(), Status>)` helper uses catch_unwind and returns STATUS_SUCCESS, the error status, or STATUS_INTERNAL_ERROR (0xC00000E5).\n   - Make `Handle` Copy. `handle(info, file_name)` returns `*(Context as *const Handle)` if non-null; otherwise it looks up the path and builds `Handle { ino, kind, opened: false }`.\n   - ZwCreateFile:\n     - Free any existing context, then call `open`.\n     - On success set Context with `Box::into_raw` and set IsDirectory.\n     - If the disposition is OPEN_IF/OVERWRITE_IF/SUPERSEDE and the file already existed, return STATUS_OBJECT_NAME_COLLISION.\n     - Map a real COLLISION error for those dispositions to STATUS_SHARING_VIOLATION.\n   - Cleanup: when `DeleteOnClose` is set, delete by path.\n   - CloseFile: if Context is non-null, take the Box, release if `opened`, and set Context to 0.\n   - Leave FindFilesWithPattern, Lock/Unlock, security and streams as None. Key Technical Concepts:\n   - **Root cause of the Windows CI crash:**\n     - The dokan crate 0.3.1 `OperationInfo::context()` does `&*(Context as *const _)` with no null check.\n     - Dokan legitimately passes `DokanFileInfo.Context == 0` for opens that never reached ZwCreateFile.\n     - The debug UB check then aborts with \"null reference produced\", ending in STATUS_STACK_BUFFER_OVERRUN.\n     - Fix: our own binding over dokan-sys that falls back to a path lookup when Context is null.\n   - **Dokan create semantics:** for FILE_SUPERSEDE, FILE_OPEN_IF and FILE_OVERWRITE_IF, an existing name returns STATUS_OBJECT_NAME_COLLISION, which Dokan treats as success (memfs does the same). A real collision for those dispositions is mapped to STATUS_SHARING_VIOLATION.\n   - **ABI:** rustc 1.99 warns that \"stdcall\" is unsupported on x64 (future hard error, rust#137018). We use `extern \"system\"` callbacks in our own repr(C) `Operations` struct that mirrors `DOKAN_OPERATIONS` field for field, then cast the pointer. dokan-sys's own stdcall warnings are capped for registry deps.\n   - **unsafe_code:** the lint is now \"deny\" crate-wide; ffi.rs alone has `#![allow(unsafe_code)]`.\n   - **FILETIME:** 100 ns ticks since 1601. `UNIX_EPOCH_TICKS = 116_444_736_000_000_000`. In SetFileTime, 0, -1 and -2 mean no change.\n   - **Tracing:** `LFS_DOKAN_TRACE=1` logs every callback with its path and status to stderr (off by default).\n   - **Earlier facts:**\n     - mem-rs#36 (https://github.com/linksplatform/mem-rs/issues/36).\n     - Windows SystemTime has 100 ns precision.\n     - fuser on macOS needs NO_REPLACE.\n     - dokan-sys is x86/x64 only.\n     - The template docs check: README needs `## Features`, `## Quick Start`, `## Configuration`, `## Contributing`, `## License`, and must keep \"Deploying API documentation\". support.\n\n[![CI/CD Pipeline](https://github.com/link-foundation/rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/workflows/CI%2FCD%20Pipeline/badge.svg)](https://github.com/link-foundation/rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/actions?workflow=CI%2FCD+Pipeline)\n[![Crates.io](https://img.shields.io/crates/v/example-sum-package-name?label=crates.io&style=flat)](https://crates.io/crates/example-sum-package-name)\n[![Docs.rs](https://img.shields.io/docsrs/example-sum-package-name?label=docs.rs&style=flat)](https://docs.rs/example-sum-package-name)\n[![Rust Version](https://img.shields.io/badge/rust-1.70%2B-blue.svg)](https://www.rust-lang.org/)\n[![Codecov](https://codecov.io/gh/link-foundation/rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/branch/main/graph/badge.svg)](https://codecov.io/gh/link-foundation/rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template)\n[![License: Unlicense](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-Unlicense-blue.svg)](http://unlicense.org/)\n\n## Features\n\n- **Rust stable support**: Works with Rust stable version\n- **Cross-platform testing**: CI runs on Ubuntu, macOS, and Windows\n- **Comprehensive testing**: Unit tests, integration tests, and doc tests\n- **Code quality**: rustfmt + Clippy with pedantic lints\n- **Pre-commit hooks**: Automated code quality checks before commits\n- **CI/CD pipeline**: GitHub Actions with multi-platform support\n- **Changelog management**: Fragment-based changelog (like Changesets/Scriv)\n- **Code coverage**: Automated coverage reports with cargo-llvm-cov and Codecov\n- **Release automation**: Automatic GitHub releases, crates.io publishing, post-publish smoke tests, and optional Docker Hub image publishing\n- **Template-safe defaults**: CI/CD skips publishing when package name is `example-sum-package-name`\n\n## Quick Start\n\n### Using This Template\n\n1. Click \"Use this template\" on GitHub to create a new repository\n2. Clone your new repository\n3. Update `Cargo.toml`:\n   - Change `name` from `example-sum-package-name` to your package name\n   - Update `description`, `repository`, and `documentation` URLs\n   - Update `[lib]` name and `[[bin]]` name\n4. Keep `Cargo.lock` committed when the project has a binary target (`[[bin]]` or `src/main.rs`)\n5. Update imports in `src/main.rs`, `tests/`, and `examples/`\n6. Build and start developing!\n\n### Development Setup\n\n```bash\n# Clone the repository\ngit clone https://github.com/link-foundation/rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template.git\ncd rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template\n\n# Build the project\ncargo build\n\n# Run tests\ncargo test\n\n# Run the CLI binary\ncargo run -- --a 3 --b 7\n\n# Run an example\ncargo run --example basic_usage\n```\n\n### Running Tests\n\n```bash\n# Run all tests\ncargo test\n\n# Run tests with verbose output\ncargo test --verbose\n\n# Run doc tests\ncargo test --doc\n\n# Run a specific test\ncargo test test_sum_positive_numbers\n\n# Run tests with output\ncargo test -- --nocapture\n```\n\nCI caps each test-matrix job at 10 minutes. `cargo test` does not provide a portable global per-test timeout, so long-running network, IO, or async tests should use explicit test-level timeouts. Repositories that adopt `cargo nextest` can configure runner deadlines with options such as `--slow-timeout` and `--leak-timeout`.\n\n### Code Quality Checks\n\n```bash\n# Format code\ncargo fmt\n\n# Check formatting (CI style)\ncargo fmt --check\n\n# Run Clippy lints\ncargo clippy --all-targets --all-features\n\n# Check file size limits (requires rust-script: ./scripts/install-rust-script.sh)\nrust-script scripts/check-file-size.rs\n\n# Check the packaged crate stays under the crates.io 10 MiB upload limit\nrust-script scripts/check-crate-size.rs\n\n# Run all checks\ncargo fmt --check && cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features && rust-script scripts/check-file-size.rs\n```\n\n## Project Structure\n\n```\n.\n├── .github/\n│   └── workflows/\n│       └── release.yml             # CI/CD pipeline configuration\n├── changelog.d/                    # Changelog fragments\n│   ├── README.md                   # Fragment instructions\n│   └── *.md                        # Individual changelog entries\n├── examples/\n│   └── basic_usage.rs              # Usage examples\n├── experiments/                    # Experiment and debug scripts\n│   ├── test-changelog-parsing.rs   # Changelog parsing validation\n│   └── test-crates-io-check.rs     # Crates.io version check validation\n├── scripts/                        # Rust scripts (via rust-script)\n│   ├── bump-version.rs             # Version bumping utility\n│   ├── check-changelog-fragment.rs # Changelog fragment validation\n│   ├── check-crate-size.rs         # Version modification detection\n│   ├── collect-changelog.rs        # Changelog collection script\n│   ├── create-changelog-fragment.rs # Changelog fragment creation\n│   ├── create-github-release.rs    # GitHub release creation\n│   ├── detect-code-changes.rs      # Code change detection for CI\n│   ├── get-bump-type.rs            # Version bump type determination\n│   ├── get-version.rs              # Version extraction from Cargo.toml\n│   ├── git-config.rs               # Git configuration for CI\n│   ├── publish-crate.rs            # Crates.io publishing\n│   ├── release-naming.rs           # Release tag/title/badge naming helpers\n│   ├── rust-paths.rs               # Rust root path detection\n│   ├── smoke-test-published-crate.rs # Install/import/run smoke test for published crates\n│   ├── version-and-commit.rs       # CI/CD version management\n│   └── wait-for-crate.rs           # Crates.io availability wait before image publishing\n├── src/\n│   ├── lib.rs                      # Library entry point\n│   ├── main.rs                     # CLI binary (uses lino-arguments)\n│   └── sum.rs                      # Sum function module\n├── tests/\n│   ├── unit_tests.rs               # Unit test entry point\n│   ├── unit/\n│   │   ├── mod.rs\n│   │   ├── sum.rs                  # Unit tests for sum function\n│   │   └── ci-cd/\n│   │       ├── mod.rs\n│   │       └── changelog_parsing.rs # CI/CD changelog parsing tests\n│   ├── integration_tests.rs        # Integration test entry point\n│   └── integration/\n│       ├── mod.rs\n│       └── sum.rs                  # CLI integration tests\n├── .gitignore                      # Git ignore patterns\n├── .pre-commit-config.yaml         # Pre-commit hooks configuration\n├── Cargo.toml                      # Project configuration\n├── CHANGELOG.md                    # Project changelog\n├── CONTRIBUTING.md                 # Contribution guidelines\n├── LICENSE                         # Unlicense (public domain)\n└── README.md                       # This file\n```\n\n## Design Choices\n\n### Example Application\n\nThe template includes a simple CLI sum application using [lino-arguments](https://github.com/link-foundation/lino-arguments) (a drop-in replacement for clap that also supports `.lenv` and `.env` files). This demonstrates:\n\n- Library module (`src/sum.rs`) with a pure function\n- CLI binary (`src/main.rs`) using `lino-arguments` for argument parsing\n- Unit tests (`tests/unit/sum.rs`) testing the function directly\n- Integration tests (`tests/integration/sum.rs`) testing the full CLI binary\n\n### Code Quality Tools\n\n- **rustfmt**: Standard Rust code formatter\n- **Clippy**: Rust linter with pedantic and nursery lints enabled\n- **Pre-commit hooks**: Automated checks before each commit\n\n### Testing Strategy\n\nThe template supports multiple levels of testing:\n\n- **Unit tests**: In `tests/unit/` directory, testing functions directly\n- **Integration tests**: In `tests/integration/` directory, testing CLI binary\n- **CI/CD tests**: In `tests/unit/ci-cd/` directory, testing CI/CD script logic\n- **Doc tests**: In documentation examples using `///` comments\n- **Examples**: In `examples/` directory (also serve as documentation)\n\nUsers can easily delete CI/CD tests in `tests/unit/ci-cd/` if not needed.\n\n### Changelog Management\n\nThis template uses a fragment-based changelog system similar to [Changesets](https://github.com/changesets/changesets) and [Scriv](https://scriv.readthedocs.io/).\n\n```bash\n# Create a changelog fragment\ntouch changelog.d/$(date +%Y%m%d_%H%M%S)_my_change.md\n\n# Edit the fragment to document your changes\n```\n\n### CI/CD Pipeline\n\nThe GitHub Actions workflow provides:\n\n1. **Change detection**: Only runs relevant jobs based on changed files\n2. **Changelog check**: Validates changelog fragments on PRs with code changes\n3. **Version check**: Prevents manual version modification in PRs\n4. **Linting**: rustfmt and Clippy checks\n5. **Test matrix**: 3 OS (Ubuntu, macOS, Windows) with Rust stable\n6. **Code coverage**: cargo-llvm-cov with Codecov upload\n7. **Building**: Release build and package validation\n8. **Auto release**: Automatic releases when changelog fragments are merged to main\n9. **Manual release**: Workflow dispatch with version bump type selection\n10. **Published crate smoke test**: Installs the just-published crate from crates.io, runs CLI entry points with captured output, and compiles a fresh dependent crate against the library\n11. **Optional Docker Hub publishing**: Pushes `latest` and version tags after the matching crates.io version is visible and smoke-tested\n12. **Documentation**: Automatic docs deployment to GitHub Pages after release\n\n#### Multi-Language Monorepos\n\nRelease scripts auto-detect the Rust layout with no extra configuration. A root `Cargo.toml` is treated as a single-language repository and keeps the plain `v<version>` tag plus `<crate> <version>` GitHub release title. A `rust/Cargo.toml` layout is treated as a multi-language monorepo and uses `rust_v<version>` tags plus `[Rust] <version>` titles so Rust releases do not collide with JavaScript or other language releases in the same GitHub Releases list.\n\nGitHub release notes include a crates.io badge that links to the exact published version page, for example `https://crates.io/crates/<crate>/<version>`.\n\n### Template-Safe Defaults\n\nThe default package name `example-sum-package-name` triggers skip logic in CI/CD scripts:\n- `publish-crate.rs` skips crates.io publishing\n- `smoke-test-published-crate.rs` skips install-from-package verification\n- `create-github-release.rs` skips GitHub release creation\n- Docker Hub publishing stays disabled unless `DOCKERHUB_IMAGE` is configured and a root `Dockerfile` exists\n\nRename the package in `Cargo.toml` to enable full CI/CD publishing.\n\n## Configuration\n\n### Updating Package Name\n\nAfter creating a repository from this template:\n\n1. Update `Cargo.toml`:\n   - Change `name` field from `example-sum-package-name`\n   - Update `repository` and `documentation` URLs\n   - Change `[lib]` name and `[[bin]]` name\n   - Keep `Cargo.lock` committed for executable crates\n\n2. Update imports:\n   - `src/main.rs`\n   - `tests/unit/sum.rs`\n   - `tests/integration/sum.rs`\n   - `examples/basic_usage.rs`\n\n3. Update badges in this `README.md`\n\n### Cargo.lock for Binary Crates\n\nThis template leaves `Cargo.lock` committed because it includes a CLI binary.\nDownstream executable crates should do the same. The CI workflow runs\n`scripts/check-cargo-lock.rs` and fails when a binary package has no\n`Cargo.lock` committed at `HEAD`.\n\nThis prevents fresh dependency resolution from changing between CI runs. It also\nkeeps cargo cache keys deterministic: without a lockfile, GitHub Actions'\n`hashFiles('**/Cargo.lock')` expression resolves to the same empty hash, so an\nunpinned dependency graph can be cached and hide resolution drift.\n\nIf the guard fails, generate the lockfile and commit it:\n\n```bash\ncargo generate-lockfile\ngit add Cargo.lock\n```\n\n### Cargo Registry Network Hardening\n\nThe release workflow sets Cargo network defaults at workflow scope so every\nCargo command, from installing rust-script through release publishing,\ninherits them:\n\n```yaml\nCARGO_NET_RETRY: '10'\nCARGO_HTTP_MULTIPLEXING: 'false'\n```\n\n`CARGO_NET_RETRY` gives transient registry index and crate-download failures\nmore chances to recover. `CARGO_HTTP_MULTIPLEXING=false` avoids libcurl HTTP/2\nmultiplexing, which can fail on GitHub-hosted runners with errors such as\n`[16] Error in the HTTP2 framing layer`.\n\n### Optional Docker Hub Publishing\n\nProjects that ship a Docker image can publish Docker Hub releases from the same Rust release workflow. Add a root `Dockerfile`, then configure:\n\n| Name | Type | Example | Purpose |\n| ---- | ---- | ------- | ------- |\n| `DOCKERHUB_IMAGE` | Repository variable | `my-dockerhub-user/my-image` | Docker Hub repository to publish |\n| `DOCKERHUB_USERNAME` | Repository variable or secret | `my-dockerhub-user` | Docker Hub login username |\n| `DOCKERHUB_TOKEN` | Repository secret | Docker Hub access token | Docker Hub login token |\n\nWhen configured, the release workflow publishes both `latest` and the Cargo package version tag, for example `my-dockerhub-user/my-image:0.10.0`. Docker publishing runs only after crates.io reports the matching version as available, and release checks rerun missing Docker Hub or GitHub release artifacts without bumping the version again.\n\nAdd a visible Docker Hub badge next to the crates.io badge in repositories that enable image publishing:\n\n```markdown\n[![Docker Hub](https://img.shields.io/docker/v/my-dockerhub-user/my-image?label=docker%20hub)](https://hub.docker.com/r/my-dockerhub-user/my-image)\n```\n\n## Deploying API documentation\n\nThe `deploy-docs` job in `.github/workflows/release.yml` publishes `cargo doc --no-deps --all-features` output to GitHub Pages on every push to `main` and on `workflow_dispatch` with `release_mode == 'instant'`. It adds a root `index.html` redirect to the generated crate documentation and a `.nojekyll` marker so rustdoc assets are served verbatim. It uses the official `actions/configure-pages` / `actions/upload-pages-artifact` / `actions/deploy-pages` flow, which requires the repository's Pages source to be set to **GitHub Actions**.\n\nBefore the first run on `main`, open **Settings → Pages** of the new repository and set **Source = GitHub Actions**. This is a one-time manual step and cannot be configured from a workflow. The `deploy-docs` job will then provision the Pages site on its first run.\n\n### Optional desktop releases\n\nSet the repository variable `DESKTOP_RELEASE_ENABLED` to `true` to enable\n`.github/workflows/desktop-release.yml`. Pull requests then dry-run a six-target\nmatrix; successful releases publish the non-empty files produced by\n`scripts/package-desktop.sh`, SLSA provenance attestations, `SHA256SUMS.txt`, and\n`BUILD-PROVENANCE.txt`. The same Pages site exposes the latest assets at\n`/download/` using the GitHub Releases API.\n\nThe included packaging hook builds the example Rust executable. Desktop\napplications should replace its implementation while retaining the\n`<target-label> <output-directory>` interface. Click \"Use this template\" on GitHub to create a new repository\n2. Clone your new repository\n3. Update `Cargo.toml`:\n   - Change `name` from `example-sum-package-name` to your package name\n   - Update `description`, `repository`, and `documentation` URLs\n   - Update `[lib]` name and `[[bin]]` name\n4. Keep `Cargo.lock` committed when the project has a binary target (`[[bin]]` or `src/main.rs`)\n5. Update imports in `src/main.rs`, `tests/`, and `examples/`\n6. Repositories that adopt `cargo nextest` can configure runner deadlines with options such as `--slow-timeout` and `--leak-timeout`.\n\n### Code Quality Checks\n\n```bash\n# Format code\ncargo fmt\n\n# Check formatting (CI style)\ncargo fmt --check\n\n# Run Clippy lints\ncargo clippy --all-targets --all-features\n\n# Check file size limits (requires rust-script: ./scripts/install-rust-script.sh)\nrust-script scripts/check-file-size.rs\n\n# Check the packaged crate stays under the crates.io 10 MiB upload limit\nrust-script scripts/check-crate-size.rs\n\n# Run all checks\ncargo fmt --check && cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features && rust-script scripts/check-file-size.rs\n```\n\n## Project Structure\n\n```\n.\n├── .github/\n│   └── workflows/\n│       └── release.yml             # This demonstrates:\n\n- Library module (`src/sum.rs`) with a pure function\n- CLI binary (`src/main.rs`) using `lino-arguments` for argument parsing\n- Unit tests (`tests/unit/sum.rs`) testing the function directly\n- Integration tests (`tests/integration/sum.rs`) testing the full CLI binary\n\n### Code Quality Tools\n\n- **rustfmt**: Standard Rust code formatter\n- **Clippy**: Rust linter with pedantic and nursery lints enabled\n- **Pre-commit hooks**: Automated checks before each commit\n\n### Testing Strategy\n\nThe template supports multiple levels of testing:\n\n- **Unit tests**: In `tests/unit/` directory, testing functions directly\n- **Integration tests**: In `tests/integration/` directory, testing CLI binary\n- **CI/CD tests**: In `tests/unit/ci-cd/` directory, testing CI/CD script logic\n- **Doc tests**: In documentation examples using `///` comments\n- **Examples**: In `examples/` directory (also serve as documentation)\n\nUsers can easily delete CI/CD tests in `tests/unit/ci-cd/` if not needed.\n\n### Changelog Management\n\nThis template uses a fragment-based changelog system similar to [Changesets](https://github.com/changesets/changesets) and [Scriv](https://scriv.readthedocs.io/).\n\n```bash\n# Create a changelog fragment\ntouch changelog.d/$(date +%Y%m%d_%H%M%S)_my_change.md\n\n# Edit the fragment to document your changes\n```\n\n### CI/CD Pipeline\n\nThe GitHub Actions workflow provides:\n\n1. **Change detection**: Only runs relevant jobs based on changed files\n2. **Changelog check**: Validates changelog fragments on PRs with code changes\n3. **Version check**: Prevents manual version modification in PRs\n4. **Linting**: rustfmt and Clippy checks\n5. **Test matrix**: 3 OS (Ubuntu, macOS, Windows) with Rust stable\n6. **Code coverage**: cargo-llvm-cov with Codecov upload\n7. **Building**: Release build and package validation\n8. **Auto release**: Automatic releases when changelog fragments are merged to main\n9. **Manual release**: Workflow dispatch with version bump type selection\n10. **Published crate smoke test**: Installs the just-published crate from crates.io, runs CLI entry points with captured output, and compiles a fresh dependent crate against the library\n11. **Optional Docker Hub publishing**: Pushes `latest` and version tags after the matching crates.io version is visible and smoke-tested\n12. **Documentation**: Automatic docs deployment to GitHub Pages after release\n\n#### Multi-Language Monorepos\n\nRelease scripts auto-detect the Rust layout with no extra configuration. A root `Cargo.toml` is treated as a single-language repository and keeps the plain `v<version>` tag plus `<crate> <version>` GitHub release title. A `rust/Cargo.toml` layout is treated as a multi-language monorepo and uses `rust_v<version>` tags plus `[Rust] <version>` titles so Rust releases do not collide with JavaScript or other language releases in the same GitHub Releases list.\n\nGitHub release notes include a crates.io badge that links to the exact published version page, for example `https://crates.io/crates/<crate>/<version>`.\n\n### Template-Safe Defaults\n\nThe default package name `example-sum-package-name` triggers skip logic in CI/CD scripts:\n- `publish-crate.rs` skips crates.io publishing\n- `smoke-test-published-crate.rs` skips install-from-package verification\n- `create-github-release.rs` skips GitHub release creation\n- Docker Hub publishing stays disabled unless `DOCKERHUB_IMAGE` is configured and a root `Dockerfile` exists\n\nRename the package in `Cargo.toml` to enable full CI/CD publishing.\n\n## Configuration\n\n### Updating Package Name\n\nAfter creating a repository from this template:\n\n1. Update `Cargo.toml`:\n   - Change `name` field from `example-sum-package-name`\n   - Update `repository` and `documentation` URLs\n   - Change `[lib]` name and `[[bin]]` name\n   - Keep `Cargo.lock` committed for executable crates\n\n2. Update imports:\n   - `src/main.rs`\n   - `tests/unit/sum.rs`\n   - `tests/integration/sum.rs`\n   - `examples/basic_usage.rs`\n\n3. Update badges in this `README.md`\n\n### Cargo.lock for Binary Crates\n\nThis template leaves `Cargo.lock` committed because it includes a CLI binary.\nDownstream executable crates should do the same. The CI workflow runs\n`scripts/check-cargo-lock.rs` and fails when a binary package has no\n`Cargo.lock` committed at `HEAD`.\n\nThis prevents fresh dependency resolution from changing between CI runs. It also\nkeeps cargo cache keys deterministic: without a lockfile, GitHub Actions'\n`hashFiles('**/Cargo.lock')` expression resolves to the same empty hash, so an\nunpinned dependency graph can be cached and hide resolution drift.\n\nIf the guard fails, generate the lockfile and commit it:\n\n```bash\ncargo generate-lockfile\ngit add Cargo.lock\n```\n\n### Cargo Registry Network Hardening\n\nThe release workflow sets Cargo network defaults at workflow scope so every\nCargo command, from installing rust-script through release publishing,\ninherits them:\n\n```yaml\nCARGO_NET_RETRY: '10'\nCARGO_HTTP_MULTIPLEXING: 'false'\n```\n\n`CARGO_NET_RETRY` gives transient registry index and crate-download failures\nmore chances to recover. `CARGO_HTTP_MULTIPLEXING=false` avoids libcurl HTTP/2\nmultiplexing, which can fail on GitHub-hosted runners with errors such as\n`[16] Error in the HTTP2 framing layer`.\n\n### Optional Docker Hub Publishing\n\nProjects that ship a Docker image can publish Docker Hub releases from the same Rust release workflow. Add a root `Dockerfile`, then configure:\n\n| Name | Type | Example | Purpose |\n| ---- | ---- | ------- | ------- |\n| `DOCKERHUB_IMAGE` | Repository variable | `my-dockerhub-user/my-image` | Docker Hub repository to publish |\n| `DOCKERHUB_USERNAME` | Repository variable or secret | `my-dockerhub-user` | Docker Hub login username |\n| `DOCKERHUB_TOKEN` | Repository secret | Docker Hub access token | Docker Hub login token |\n\nWhen configured, the release workflow publishes both `latest` and the Cargo package version tag, for example `my-dockerhub-user/my-image:0.10.0`. Docker publishing runs only after crates.io reports the matching version as available, and release checks rerun missing Docker Hub or GitHub release artifacts without bumping the version again.\n\nAdd a visible Docker Hub badge next to the crates.io badge in repositories that enable image publishing:\n\n```markdown\n[![Docker Hub](https://img.shields.io/docker/v/my-dockerhub-user/my-image?label=docker%20hub)](https://hub.docker.com/r/my-dockerhub-user/my-image)\n```\n\n## Deploying API documentation\n\nThe `deploy-docs` job in `.github/workflows/release.yml` publishes `cargo doc --no-deps --all-features` output to GitHub Pages on every push to `main` and on `workflow_dispatch` with `release_mode == 'instant'`. It adds a root `index.html` redirect to the generated crate documentation and a `.nojekyll` marker so rustdoc assets are served verbatim. It uses the official `actions/configure-pages` / `actions/upload-pages-artifact` / `actions/deploy-pages` flow, which requires the repository's Pages source to be set to **GitHub Actions**.\n\nBefore the first run on `main`, open **Settings → Pages** of the new repository and set **Source = GitHub Actions**. This is a one-time manual step and cannot be configured from a workflow. The `deploy-docs` job will then provision the Pages site on its first run.\n\n### Optional desktop releases\n\nSet the repository variable `DESKTOP_RELEASE_ENABLED` to `true` to enable\n`.github/workflows/desktop-release.yml`. Pull requests then dry-run a six-target\nmatrix; successful releases publish the non-empty files produced by\n`scripts/package-desktop.sh`, SLSA provenance attestations, `SHA256SUMS.txt`, and\n`BUILD-PROVENANCE.txt`. The same Pages site exposes the latest assets at\n`/download/` using the GitHub Releases API.\n\nThe included packaging hook builds the example Rust executable. Desktop\napplications should replace its implementation while retaining the\n`<target-label> <output-directory>` interface. For electron-builder 26 macOS\nad-hoc builds, pass `-c.mac.identity=-`, retain `CSC_FOR_PULL_REQUEST=true` for\nthe PR dry run, and emit an app with\n`Contents/_CodeSignature/CodeResources`; the workflow smoke test rejects an\nunwrapped `.app` directory.\n\nIf this step is skipped, the first `deploy-docs` run fails on `actions/deploy-pages@v5` with `Error: Get Pages site failed.` / `Error: Failed to create deployment`. Flip the Pages source as described above and re-run the failed job; no workflow changes are required.\n\n## Scripts Reference\n\nAll scripts in `scripts/` are Rust scripts that use [rust-script](https://github.com/fornwall/rust-script).\nInstall rust-script with: `./scripts/install-rust-script.sh`\n\n| Command                               | Description              |\n| ------------------------------------- | ------------------------ |\n| `cargo test`                          | Run all tests            |\n| `cargo fmt`                           | Format code              |\n| `cargo clippy`                        | Run lints                |\n| `cargo run -- --a 3 --b 7`           | Run CLI (sum 3 + 7)     |\n| `cargo run --example basic_usage`     | Run example              |\n| `rust-script scripts/check-cargo-lock.rs` | Require committed Cargo.lock for binary crates |\n| `rust-script scripts/check-file-size.rs` | Check file size limits |\n| `rust-script scripts/check-crate-size.rs` | Check crate archive size (crates.io 10 MiB limit) |\n| `rust-script scripts/smoke-test-published-crate.rs --release-version <version>` | Verify the published crates.io artifact from a clean install |\n| `rust-script scripts/bump-version.rs` | Bump version             |\n\n## Example Usage\n\n```rust\nuse example_sum_package_name::sum;\n\nfn main() {\n    let result = sum(2, 3);\n    println!(\"2 + 3 = {result}\");\n}\n```\n\nSee `examples/basic_usage.rs` for more examples.\n\n## Contributing\n\nContributions are welcome! There is no allocation bitmap: free space is rebuilt at mount from the\n//! owners listed here (journal, chunk tables, chunks) and from the file\n//! extents in the inode records.\n=== src/space.rs\n//! Block allocator.\n//!\n//! The allocation state is not stored on disk: it is rebuilt at mount from\n//! the owners of every block (superblock, journal, chunk tables, chunks and\n//! file extents). This removes a whole class of bitmap/metadata mismatches,\n//! and every block always has exactly one owner, which the disk map shows.\n//!\n//! Blocks freed since the last commit stay reserved until the commit lands\n//! (\"pending free\"), so a crash can never expose a reused block to the old\n//! committed metadata. Blocks allocated since the last commit are \"fresh\":\n//! writing them needs no journaling because no committed structure refers to\n//! them yet.\n=== src/chunked.rs\n//! Relocatable arrays of fixed-size records.\n//!\n//! Links, inodes, usage handles and every size class of the variable-size\n//! store are [`ChunkedArray`]s: records live in small chunks (one block, or\n//! one record when records are larger than a block) that can sit anywhere on\n//! the device. Chunks are what fills the gaps between contiguous files, and\n//! they are \"liquid\": the allocator may move a chunk to let a file grow in\n//! place. A chunk table (one `u64` block number per chunk) stored in its own\n//! contiguous extent locates the chunks.\n//!\n//! New chunks get their blocks only at commit (delayed allocation), so the\n//! allocator sees the final set of new chunks at once and places each of\n//! them in the smallest gap.\n=== src/journal.rs\n//! The optional write-ahead journal shared by the file system and the links\n//! database.\n//!\n//! The journal is a fixed region (blocks `start..start + blocks`) holding at\n//! most one transaction at a time, always written from the region start:\n//!\n//! ```text\n//! descriptor block(s)  \"LFSJDESC\" seq count | target block numbers...\n//! data blocks          new contents of each target, in order\n//! commit block         \"LFSJCMIT\" seq count crc32(descriptors + data)\n//! ```\n//!\n//! A transaction is durable once its commit block is on disk. On mount it is\n//! replayed if it is valid and its sequence number is the superblock's plus\n//! one (or the superblock is torn and the transaction carries block 0).\n//! Replaying is idempotent, so a crash during replay is harmless. Because the\n//! superblock (block 0) is always checkpointed last, a superblock carrying\n//! the new sequence number implies every other block is checkpointed too.\n=== src/varstore.rs\n//! Variable-size storage: power-of-two size classes from 16 bytes to 1 MiB.\n//!\n//! Every class is a [`ChunkedArray`] of fixed-size slots, so variable-size\n//! objects never fragment the device: they live in the same small,\n//! relocatable chunks as links. A slot starts with a `u32` length; length 0\n//! marks a free slot (free slots are found again at mount by that marker).\n//!\n//! Objects are addressed by a [`Handle`] that packs a kind tag, the class and\n//! the slot number into one `u64`, so a handle fits in a link-sized cell.\n=== src/sbt.rs\n//! Size-balanced trees over externally stored nodes.\n//!\n//! The same algorithm (Chen Qifeng's SBT, as used by linksplatform's\n//! doublets) drives the trees embedded in link records and the per-link\n//! trees of the optional variable-size index. Node `0` is the null node;\n//! subtree sizes are plain counts, so a tree is byte-compatible with the\n//! doublets `size_as_source`/`size_as_target` cells.\n=== src/codec.rs\n//! Little-endian field helpers and CRC-32 used by every on-disk structure.\n//!\n//! All multi-byte integers are stored little-endian, so images are portable\n//! between machines (the doublets store uses native endianness, which is\n//! little-endian on every platform LFS targets).\n=== src/device.rs\n//! Block devices: where an LFS image lives.\n//!\n//! The file system addresses the device in whole blocks. [`FileDevice`] works\n//! with regular image files and raw devices (`/dev/sdb1`, `\\\\.\\E:`) on every\n//! platform, [`MemDevice`] keeps the image in memory (tests, the web\n//! visualizer) and [`CrashDevice`] simulates power loss for journal tests.\n=== src/links/mod.rs\n//! The embedded universal links database.\n//!\n//! A doublets store (every link is `index: source -> target`) shared by the\n//! file system and by users through the CLI and the `/.lfs` directory. The\n//! file system's own structures — inodes, names, directory entries — are\n//! ordinary links of this store, so one journal covers both.\n//!\n//! Values that are not link indices are stored as *external references*\n//! using the `Platform.Data.Hybrid` encoding of binary links notation: the\n//! external value `v` is the raw cell `2^64 - v` (and external zero is\n//! `2^63`), so internal indices are `1..2^63`.\n=== src/links/packet.rs\n//! Import and export of the links store.\n//!\n//! * **Store archive** — the whole store in [binary links notation] version 1,\n//!   exactly as link-cli writes it (`--export-binary`, spec §10): a links\n//!   packet without external references and with packed widths, where every\n//!   link keeps its address and unused addresses are section gaps, followed\n//!   by a names packet (external references, packed widths) holding\n//!   `address code-point…` per named link. The raw cells of external\n//!   references are 64-bit Hybrid values (`2^64 - v`), so they travel as\n//!   8-byte references and come back unchanged.\n//! * **Doublets file** — the `.links` file of the doublets library\n//!   (`UnitedMemoryLinks<u64>`): 64-byte records, the header in record 0.\n//!   It is byte for byte the record array of the united layout.\n//! * **`LiNo` text** — one `(index: source target)` link per line, with `$v`\n//!   for the external value `v`.\n//!\n//! [`Links::place_all`] imports at the original addresses (into a store\n//! where they are free); [`import_remapped`] gives the links new addresses\n//! and reuses links that already exist, which is how a mounted volume\n//! takes foreign links without touching its own.\n//!\n//! [binary links notation]: https://github.com/link-foundation/links-notation/blob/main/docs/protocol/binary-links-notation.md\n=== src/links/usage.rs\n//! The optional variable-size usage index.\n//!\n//! For every link `X` and each role it keeps the set of links that use `X`\n//! as their source (or target). A set is stored in the variable-size store\n//! either as a size-balanced tree (24 bytes per user) or as a bit string\n//! (one bit per link in the store, bit `L` set iff link `L` uses `X`).\n//!\n//! In adaptive mode the encoding is chosen per set by usage density\n//! `users / links`: a bit string costs `links / 8` bytes and a tree\n//! `24 * users`, so the break-even density is 1/192. Above the threshold a\n//! set becomes a bit string; it goes back to a tree only when the density\n//! drops below `threshold * hysteresis` so sets near the boundary do not\n//! flip back and forth.\n=== src/fs/mod.rs\n//! The file system: files and directories stored as links.\n//!\n//! # Schema\n//!\n//! Links `1..=5` are the binary links notation marker points (`ONE`,\n//! `NUMBER`, `STRING`, `LIST`, `IDENTIFIED`); `6..=9` are the type points\n//! [`FILE`], [`DIR`], [`SYMLINK`] and [`CONFIG`]. Then:\n//!\n//! ```text\n//! inode     I = (TYPE, $slot)        slot of the 64-byte inode record\n//! name      N = (STRING, chain)      binary links notation string\n//! entry     E = (D, N)               name N in directory D\n//! binding   B = (E, I)               the entry points at inode I\n//! symlink   S = (I, N)               symbolic link I points at text N\n//! config    C = (CONFIG, N)          persisted runtime configuration\n//! ```\n//!\n//! Because a link is unique by its source and target, a name exists at most\n//! once per directory and every name text is stored once per volume. Hard\n//! links are several bindings of one inode; the parent of a directory is\n//! found from its only binding.\n//!\n//! # Data\n//!\n//! Every file is one contiguous extent. Growing tries, in order: growth in\n//! place (with `growth-percent` extra room), exact growth in place, moving\n//! the link chunks that block growth in place, relocating the file, and\n//! compacting the volume. Link, inode and index chunks fill the gaps between\n//! files, so the volume never fragments.\n=== src/fs/commit.rs\n//! Commit: one atomic transaction for the file system and the links\n//! database together.\n//!\n//! 1. New chunks get blocks (link chunks go into the smallest gaps when\n//!    `gap-fill` is on).\n//! 2. Blocks allocated since the last commit (\"fresh\") are written in place:\n//!    no committed structure refers to them, so a crash cannot expose them.\n//! 3. Overwrites of committed blocks and the new superblock go through the\n//!    journal, then are checkpointed in place, superblock last. If they do\n//!    not fit, the dirty chunks are first moved to fresh blocks\n//!    (copy-on-write), which leaves only the chunk tables and the superblock\n//!    to journal.\n//! 4. Without a journal every dirty chunk and table is moved to fresh blocks\n//!    instead, so only the superblock is overwritten in place.\n=== src/fs/control.rs\n//! The virtual `.lfs` control directory in the root of every mounted volume.\n//!\n//! * `.lfs/config` — the runtime configuration as links notation; writing\n//!   `(key: value)` lines and closing the file applies them immediately,\n//!   without remounting.\n//! * `.lfs/map.json` — the disk space map read by the web visualizer.\n//! * `.lfs/links` — every link of the embedded database as links notation.\n//! * `.lfs/stats` — volume statistics.\n//!\n//! The entries are not stored on the device; their inode numbers sit at the\n//! top of the inode number space where no real inode can reach.\n=== src/fs/map.rs\n//! The disk space map: who owns every block.\n//!\n//! Every block has exactly one owner (superblock, journal, a chunk table, a\n//! chunk of one of the arrays, or one file extent), is free, or is pending\n//! (freed since the last commit). The map is what the web visualizer draws.\n=== src/fs/file.rs\n//! File data: one contiguous extent per file.\n//!\n//! [2026-10-22T00:35:06.369Z] [INFO]           "command": "python3 - <<'PY'\ns=open('README.md').read()\nkeep=s[s.index('## Deploying API documentation'):s.index('## Scripts Reference')]\nkeep=keep.replace(\"The `deploy-docs` job in `.github/workflows/release.yml` publishes `cargo doc --no-deps --all-features` output to GitHub Pages\",\"The `deploy-docs` job in `.github/workflows/release.yml` publishes `cargo doc --no-deps --all-features` output and the disk-space map visualizer (`/visualizer/`) to GitHub Pages\")\nkeep=keep.replace(\"The included packaging hook builds the example Rust executable.\",\"The included packaging hook builds the `lfs` executable.\")\nhead='''# LFS — the links file system\n\nA file system driver in Rust for Linux, macOS and Windows whose metadata is\nan embedded [doublets](https://github.com/linksplatform/doublets-rs) links\ndatabase. The file system and the database share one optional journal, every\nfile is one contiguous extent, and the gaps between files are filled with\nlink chunks, so the volume does not fragment.\n\n[![CI/CD Pipeline](https://github.com/link-foundation/lfs/workflows/CI%2FCD%20Pipeline/badge.svg)](https://github.com/link-foundation/lfs/actions?workflow=CI%2FCD+Pipeline)\n[![Crates.io](https://img.shields.io/crates/v/links-fs?label=crates.io&style=flat)](https://crates.io/crates/links-fs)\n[![Docs.rs](https://img.shields.io/docsrs/links-fs?label=docs.rs&style=flat)](https://docs.rs/links-fs)\n[![Rust Version](https://img.shields.io/badge/rust-1.87%2B-blue.svg)](https://www.rust-lang.org/)\n[![License: Unlicense](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-Unlicense-blue.svg)](http://unlicense.org/)\n\n![The disk-space map of a volume with gaps between files](docs/screenshots/visualizer-gaps.png)\n\n## Features\n\n- **One store for everything.** Inodes, names, directory entries and\n  symbolic links are ordinary links of a doublets store\n  (`index: source -> target`). Users create, query, import and export their\n  own links in the same store. One commit is one atomic transaction for both.\n- **One optional journal.** Its modes are `off`, `metadata` and `full`, so the\n  links database is never journaled twice (\"journaling of journal\").\n- **No fragmentation.** Every file is one contiguous extent. Links, inodes and\n  index nodes live in small relocatable chunks that fill the gaps between\n  files. Online compaction moves everything down so the free space is one\n  extent again.\n- **Configurable layout.** The format can be the united doublets layout\n  (64-byte records, byte-compatible with `UnitedMemoryLinks<u64>`), the split\n  layout (16-byte data and a 48-byte index), or data only.\n- **Variable-size index.** Each link's set of users is kept either as a\n  size-balanced tree or as an experimental bit string. In `adaptive` mode the\n  set switches at a density threshold (`auto` = 1/192), with hysteresis.\n- **Runtime configuration.** Journal mode, allocator, gap filling, index\n  mode, threshold, compaction and more change without reformatting. They are\n  stored in links notation inside the volume, so an external drive carries\n  its settings. They can also be changed live through `/.lfs/config`.\n- **Binary links notation.** Names are binary links notation strings. The\n  whole store imports and exports as binary links notation archives (as\n  link-cli writes them), doublets `.links` files, or LiNo text.\n- **Portable images.** Images are little-endian on regular files or raw\n  devices, mountable with FUSE (Linux, FreeBSD, macOS with macFUSE) and\n  Dokan 2 (Windows x64).\n- **Disk-space map.** `lfs map` and `/.lfs/map.json` say who owns every\n  block. The [visualizer](https://link-foundation.github.io/lfs/visualizer/)\n  on GitHub Pages draws it.\n- **Crash safety.** The allocation state is rebuilt from block owners at\n  mount, so there is no bitmap to disagree with. Freed blocks stay reserved\n  until the commit lands. `lfs fsck` checks every invariant.\n\n## Quick Start\n\n```bash\ncargo install links-fs            # the `lfs` command line tool\n\nlfs mkfs disk.lfs --size 64M --label demo\nlfs put disk.lfs notes.txt /      # copy host files in (directories with -r)\nlfs ls disk.lfs /\nlfs cat disk.lfs /notes.txt\nlfs get disk.lfs /notes.txt copy.txt\n\nlfs links disk.lfs point          # (245: 245 245)\nlfs links disk.lfs create 245 '$7'\nlfs links disk.lfs --source 245   # query the embedded links database\nlfs export-links disk.lfs store.lino\n\nlfs compact disk.lfs              # defragment the free space\nlfs map disk.lfs > map.json       # open it in the visualizer\nlfs fsck disk.lfs\n```\n\n### Mounting\n\n```bash\ncargo install links-fs --features fuse    # Linux, FreeBSD, macOS\nlfs mount disk.lfs /mnt/lfs               # Ctrl-C unmounts and commits\necho '(journal: off)' > /mnt/lfs/.lfs/config\n\ncargo install links-fs --features dokan   # Windows x64\nlfs mount disk.lfs M:\n```\n\n| Platform | Driver | Needs at run time |\n| -------- | ------ | ----------------- |\n| Linux, FreeBSD | FUSE (`fuser`, pure Rust) | `fusermount3` (`apt install fuse3`) |\n| macOS | FUSE | [macFUSE](https://osxfuse.github.io/) (also needed to build) |\n| Windows x64 | Dokan 2 (own binding over `dokan-sys`) | [Dokan 2](https://github.com/dokan-dev/dokany/releases) |\n\nEvery mounted volume has a virtual `.lfs` directory with four files:\n`config` (write `(key: value)` lines to apply them), `map.json`, `links` and\n`stats`. Set `LFS_DOKAN_TRACE=1` on Windows to log every Dokan callback to\nstandard error.\n\n### As a library\n\n```rust\nuse links_fs::config::FormatOptions;\nuse links_fs::device::MemDevice;\nuse links_fs::fs::{Creator, Fs, ROOT_INO};\n\nlet mut fs = Fs::format(MemDevice::new(4 << 20), &FormatOptions::default(), \"demo\")?;\nfs.set_config_value(\"index\", \"adaptive\")?;\nlet ino = fs.create(ROOT_INO, \"hello.txt\", 0o644, Creator::default())?.ino;\nfs.write(ino, 0, b\"Hello, links!\")?;\nlet link = fs.create_link(fs.create_point()?, fs.create_point()?)?;\nfs.commit()?;\n```\n\n`cargo run --example basic_usage` runs the full example\n(`examples/basic_usage.rs`). It covers user links, compaction and the space\nmap.\n\n### Development\n\n```bash\ncargo build --all-features\ncargo test --all-features         # unit, integration and FUSE mount tests\ncargo fmt --check\ncargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings\nrust-script scripts/check-file-size.rs\nbash experiments/fuse_smoke.sh    # mount an image and use it with coreutils\nbash experiments/issue-1-cross-check.sh   # clippy for windows-gnu and macOS\n```\n\nThe FUSE mount tests skip when `/dev/fuse` is missing, unless\n`LFS_REQUIRE_FUSE=1` is set. The Windows tests do the same unless\n`LFS_REQUIRE_DOKAN=1` is set. The file system and the database share one optional journal, every\nfile is one contiguous extent, and the gaps between files are filled with\nlink chunks, so the volume does not fragment.\n\n[![CI/CD Pipeline](https://github.com/link-foundation/lfs/workflows/CI%2FCD%20Pipeline/badge.svg)](https://github.com/link-foundation/lfs/actions?workflow=CI%2FCD+Pipeline)\n[![Crates.io](https://img.shields.io/crates/v/links-fs?label=crates.io&style=flat)](https://crates.io/crates/links-fs)\n[![Docs.rs](https://img.shields.io/docsrs/links-fs?label=docs.rs&style=flat)](https://docs.rs/links-fs)\n[![Rust Version](https://img.shields.io/badge/rust-1.87%2B-blue.svg)](https://www.rust-lang.org/)\n[![License: Unlicense](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-Unlicense-blue.svg)](http://unlicense.org/)\n\n![The disk-space map of a volume with gaps between files](docs/screenshots/visualizer-gaps.png)\n\n## Features\n\n- **One store for everything.** Inodes, names, directory entries and\n  symbolic links are ordinary links of a doublets store\n  (`index: source -> target`). Users create, query, import and export their\n  own links in the same store. One commit is one atomic transaction for both.\n- **One optional journal.** Its modes are `off`, `metadata` and `full`, so the\n  links database is never journaled twice (\"journaling of journal\").\n- **No fragmentation.** Every file is one contiguous extent. Links, inodes and\n  index nodes live in small relocatable chunks that fill the gaps between\n  files. Online compaction moves everything down so the free space is one\n  extent again.\n- **Configurable layout.** The format can be the united doublets layout\n  (64-byte records, byte-compatible with `UnitedMemoryLinks<u64>`), the split\n  layout (16-byte data and a 48-byte index), or data only.\n- **Variable-size index.** Each link's set of users is kept either as a\n  size-balanced tree or as an experimental bit string. In `adaptive` mode the\n  set switches at a density threshold (`auto` = 1/192), with hysteresis.\n- **Runtime configuration.** Journal mode, allocator, gap filling, index\n  mode, threshold, compaction and more change without reformatting. They are\n  stored in links notation inside the volume, so an external drive carries\n  its settings. They can also be changed live through `/.lfs/config`.\n- **Binary links notation.** Names are binary links notation strings. The\n  whole store imports and exports as binary links notation archives (as\n  link-cli writes them), doublets `.links` files, or LiNo text.\n- **Portable images.** Images are little-endian on regular files or raw\n  devices, mountable with FUSE (Linux, FreeBSD, macOS with macFUSE) and\n  Dokan 2 (Windows x64).\n- **Disk-space map.** `lfs map` and `/.lfs/map.json` say who owns every\n  block. The [visualizer](https://link-foundation.github.io/lfs/visualizer/)\n  on GitHub Pages draws it.\n- **Crash safety.** The allocation state is rebuilt from block owners at\n  mount, so there is no bitmap to disagree with. Freed blocks stay reserved\n  until the commit lands. `lfs fsck` checks every invariant.\n\n## Quick Start\n\n```bash\ncargo install links-fs            # the `lfs` command line tool\n\nlfs mkfs disk.lfs --size 64M --label demo\nlfs put disk.lfs notes.txt /      # copy host files in (directories with -r)\nlfs ls disk.lfs /\nlfs cat disk.lfs /notes.txt\nlfs get disk.lfs /notes.txt copy.txt\n\nlfs links disk.lfs point          # (245: 245 245)\nlfs links disk.lfs create 245 '$7'\nlfs links disk.lfs --source 245   # query the embedded links database\nlfs export-links disk.lfs store.lino\n\nlfs compact disk.lfs              # defragment the free space\nlfs map disk.lfs > map.json       # open it in the visualizer\nlfs fsck disk.lfs\n```\n\n### Mounting\n\n```bash\ncargo install links-fs --features fuse    # Linux, FreeBSD, macOS\nlfs mount disk.lfs /mnt/lfs               # Ctrl-C unmounts and commits\necho '(journal: off)' > /mnt/lfs/.lfs/config\n\ncargo install links-fs --features dokan   # Windows x64\nlfs mount disk.lfs M:\n```\n\n| Platform | Driver | Needs at run time |\n| -------- | ------ | ----------------- |\n| Linux, FreeBSD | FUSE (`fuser`, pure Rust) | `fusermount3` (`apt install fuse3`) |\n| macOS | FUSE | [macFUSE](https://osxfuse.github.io/) (also needed to build) |\n| Windows x64 | Dokan 2 (own binding over `dokan-sys`) | [Dokan 2](https://github.com/dokan-dev/dokany/releases) |\n\nEvery mounted volume has a virtual `.lfs` directory with four files:\n`config` (write `(key: value)` lines to apply them), `map.json`, `links` and\n`stats`. Set `LFS_DOKAN_TRACE=1` on Windows to log every Dokan callback to\nstandard error.\n\n### As a library\n\n```rust\nuse links_fs::config::FormatOptions;\nuse links_fs::device::MemDevice;\nuse links_fs::fs::{Creator, Fs, ROOT_INO};\n\nlet mut fs = Fs::format(MemDevice::new(4 << 20), &FormatOptions::default(), \"demo\")?;\nfs.set_config_value(\"index\", \"adaptive\")?;\nlet ino = fs.create(ROOT_INO, \"hello.txt\", 0o644, Creator::default())?.ino;\nfs.write(ino, 0, b\"Hello, links!\")?;\nlet link = fs.create_link(fs.create_point()?, fs.create_point()?)?;\nfs.commit()?;\n```\n\n`cargo run --example basic_usage` runs the full example\n(`examples/basic_usage.rs`).
